title: yelmox
text: The YelmoX program: one ice-sheet domain with FastIsostasy bedrock, a shared barystatic sea level, a climate backend chosen at runtime, a surface mass balance and the marine shelf, built on the multigrid kryos_domain (see Multigrid coupling). Its variant yelmox_bipolar runs two domains, north and south, coupled through the sea level and an ocean box model.

title: yelmox
text:
Stepping order
The driver owns the timeline (ts) and the shared sea level (bsl), and advances the domain once per step with the coupling sequence written out in the time loop:
call step_relax(dom, ts)          ! topography relaxation (relax)
call step_optimize(dom, ts)       ! cb_ref/tf_corr optimization (opt)
call step_isostasy(dom, ts, bsl)  ! bedrock + sea level (dt_isos cadence)
call couple_to_yelmo(dom)         ! bedrock now; smb + shelf melt lag one step
call step_ice_bnd(dom, ts, idx)   ! prescribed ice in the fixed/relaxation cells ([ice_bnd])
call step_icesheet(dom, ts)       ! yelmo_update
call couple_yelmo_to_htopo(dom)   ! hi-res geometry from the models
call step_climate(dom, ts, idx)   ! climate (dt_clim cadence)
call step_surface(dom, ts)        ! surface mass balance + temperature
call step_shelf(dom, ts)          ! shelf-base melt + temperature
couple_to_yelmo assembles the Yelmo boundary state: isostasy from this step, smb and shelf melt from the previous step (a one-step coupling lag); step_climate, step_surface and step_shelf then produce the forcing consumed on the next step. The climate is refreshed on the comps.dt_clim cadence, isostasy on the comps.dt_isos cadence (the bedrock is held in between); the smb every step.

title: yelmox
text:
Forcing: series and terms ([forcing], [series_<name>], [term_<name>])
The forcing of a run is one equation set, and the par file is its transcription (design: docs/_forcing-terms.md). At the forcing time τ = time_rel (set by [ctrl] tstep_method: const holds tstep_const, rel is the model time, cal the calendar), the climate is a reference snapshot plus terms, each a scalar series on τ times a pattern:
T^sl(x,m,τ) = T_0^sl + Σ_k α_k(τ) [T_k1^sl − T_k0^sl]          + Σ_u f_ta,u α_u(τ)
P^sl(x,m,τ) = P_0^sl · Π_k [1 + α_k(τ) (P_k1^sl/P_k0^sl − 1)]  · Π_u exp(β_p f_ta,u α_u(τ))
Θ(x,z,τ)    = Θ_0 (or the series of a replace term) + Σ_k α_k [Θ_k1 − Θ_k0] + Σ_u f_to,u α_u
S(x,z,τ)    = S_0 (or ...)                          + Σ_k α_k [S_k1 − S_k0] + Σ_u f_so,u α_u
at sea level (the snapshots reduced with the lapse rates Γ and β_p of [snapshots]), then moved to the model surface; k are the terms with a snapshots pattern, u those with a uniform pattern. The rules are fixed by field: tas, to, so add, pr multiplies (the ratio of the snapshots; in a uniform term exp(β_p ΔT)). A term without snap0 adds snap1 itself (a given anomaly or ratio). The same equations hold for every backend that takes terms (snapshots; rembo takes the uniform tas terms as its summer anomaly; esm takes ocean terms at the shelf base).
&forcing
    reference = "pd"                 ! the reference snapshot [snapshot_pd]
    series    = "glacial" "dTo"      ! [series_glacial], [series_dTo]
    terms     = "glacial" "ocean"    ! [term_glacial], [term_ocean]
    var_defs  = "input/clim_db.nml" "input/forcing_db.nml"   ! the default
/

&series_glacial                      ! a tsgen series (unset keys: template [series])
    method      = "series"
    series_file = "input/alpha_combined_125kyr_interp.dat"
/

&series_dTo                          ! derived: set by the climate each update
    method = "derived"
    from   = "air_anomaly"           ! factor x mean sea-level air anomaly over region
    factor = 0.25
    region = "all"
    units  = "K"
/

&term_glacial                        ! tas + f (lgm - picontrol), pr (1 + f (lgm/picontrol - 1))
    series = "glacial"
    snap0  = "picontrol"
    snap1  = "lgm"
    fields = "tas" "pr"
/

&term_ocean                          ! to + dTo at every depth
    series  = "dTo"
    pattern = "uniform"
    fields  = "to"
/
This reads T = T_pd + α (T_lgm − T_pic), P = P_pd [1 + α (P_lgm/P_pic − 1)], Θ = Θ_pd + 0.25 ⟨T^sl − T^sl_pd⟩ (Greenland paleo A). The library input/forcing_db.nml holds these groups (Forcing library), so a par file lists names; an experiment adds or removes terms with -p forcing.terms==glacial,ocean.
Series are named scalars on the forcing time, driver-owned: the program holds one registry (indices_class, idx, libs/kryos_forcing.f90), advances every series once per step and passes it to step_climate (and the cold start); a multi-domain driver shares one registry. Each is a tsgen time-series generator (method: const, ramp-slope, ramp-time, ramp-time-step, sin, series from a table or netCDF file, optionally normalised with norm_t0/norm_t1 to 0 at t0 and 1 at t1, each one time or a window t0 t1 whose mean is taken, exp, the PI/PID feedback controllers on the response, the ice volume in Gt; see the fesm-utils tsgen docs), or derived (method = "derived"), computed by the model after the atmosphere of the update is composed:



from
value
keys




air_anomaly
factor × the mean over region of the sea-level annual air temperature anomaly of this update (no lag; without the lapse-rate cooling of the ice sheet)
factor, region


obm_north, obm_south
the box temperature of the bipolar ocean box model, minus its initial value with anomaly = True (yelmox_bipolar)
anomaly



A term on a derived series may touch to and so only (an error at init otherwise); air_anomaly needs a backend with a sea-level air temperature (snapshots). region is "all" or a selection expression of the domain’s regions on the climate grid ([regions], e.g. "zone:open_ocean", "~zone:land"; see the fesm-utils regions docs); its cell count is printed at init. The run stops when a series trips its kill switch (with_kill), and writes a restart bundle restart-<n> each time a series moves by more than its restart_every_df. Each tsgen series restarts from series_<name>_restart.nc in the bundle (a derived one is recomputed); every series is written to the 1D output as series_<name> (tsgen ones also series_<name>_df_dt), labelled with units.
Terms are one series times one pattern on an explicit list of fields:








pattern
adds
keys




snapshots (default)
α (snap1 − snap0), or α snap1 with snap0 = "" (a sea-level anomaly or ratio, e.g. a reconstruction in time)
snap0, snap1, fields


uniform
f_ta α to tas (and exp(β_p f_ta α) to pr), f_to α to to, f_so α to so
fields, f_ta, f_to, f_so (default 1)


replace
the field = α at every depth, in place of the reference; the other terms add to it
fields (to, so), one per field



series = "" is the constant 1 (the full anomaly of a reconstruction). The snapshots of a run are the reference and the snap0/snap1 of its terms: no list. Checked at init, with an error naming the term: every series and snapshot named exists, every field is bound by its snapshots and the reference, a replace once per field, a derived series on the ocean only; a backend that supplies the smb (esm with surface_method = "climate") refuses terms on tas/pr. The value of each term’s series is written to the climate’s 2D file as term_<name>.
Order of a climate update: the backend composes the atmosphere with the snapshot terms, then the uniform terms on tas/pr; the derived series are set (air_anomaly from the composed sea-level temperature); then the ocean terms (replace, then snapshot and uniform); then the transforms [taper] and [bias]; then the move to the surface grid’s elevation. The ocean terms are re-applied by yelmox_bipolar after the box model sets its series.
Every named group (series_, term_, snapshot_ and the varslice groups of the fields, the taper weight, the bias fields, the ice history) is read from the par file if it has it, else from the first [forcing] var_defs file that does; unset keys come from the templates of input/yelmox_defaults.nml (Configuration).

title: yelmox
text:
Regional taper to the reference ([taper])
The climate transform after the terms and before [bias]: the atmosphere towards the reference climate with a static weight field w in [0, 1] on the climate grid,
now = ref + w*(now - ref)
for the monthly air temperature and precipitation, their annual means and the sea-level air temperature (those the backend supplies); w = 1 keeps the climate, w = 0 is the reference (e.g. outside the coverage of a reconstruction). The reference is taken at the current surface: a reference at its own elevation (snapshots: the surface of the reference snapshot) is moved there with the backend’s monthly lapse rate and beta_p, as the climate itself. The ocean is unchanged. Refused for a backend without a reference atmosphere (rembo).
outside sets the climate where w < 1:

"ref" (default): towards the reference, as above;
"mean": towards the reference plus the mean anomaly of the cells with w = 1, per month,
tas = tas_ref + w*(tas - tas_ref) + (1 - w)*dT(m)
pr  = w*pr + (1 - w)*pr_ref*f(m)
with dT(m) the mean temperature difference and f(m) the ratio of the precipitation totals over the cells with w = 1 (both against the reference at the current surface); ta_ann and tsl_ann take the mean of dT(m), pr_ann the ratio of the annual totals. A weight without cells at w = 1 stops the run.

&taper
    active   = True
    weight   = "taper_w"  ! group of w [1]: one 2D field (time = 0 0 0 0 1); the par file, then [forcing] var_defs
    outside  = "ref"      ! ref | mean: where w < 1, towards the reference (plus the mean anomaly of the cells with w = 1)
/
The weight is a varslice group on the climate grid or remapped online (remap, grid_src); values outside [0, 1] (or missing) stop the run. It is written to the climate’s 2D file (taper_w). input/clim_db.nml holds taper_b18_b20, the weight of the Greenland reconstructions on GreenlandPaleo (1 in their coverage, 0 beyond 100 km; outside = "mean" in grlpal_recon of scripts/grl-paleo/params.sh).

title: yelmox
text:
Climate bias correction ([bias])
A spatial correction of the atmosphere, the last climate transform, applied on the climate grid to the monthly air temperature and precipitation of any backend except rembo (annual fields only), before the move to the surface grid’s elevation:
tas = tas + f_tas*dtas,    pr = pr*(1 + f_pr*(fpr - 1))
The annual means follow (temperature additively, precipitation by the ratio of the annual totals); the reference climate and the ocean are unchanged. The group is optional; without it, or with active = False, nothing changes.
&bias
    active   = True
    dtas     = "bias_dtas"    ! group: temperature correction [K]; "" = none (the par file, then [forcing] var_defs)
    fpr      = "bias_fpr"     ! group: precipitation factor [1]; "" = none
    f_tas    = 1.0            ! weight of dtas
    f_pr     = 1.0            ! weight of fpr
/
dtas and fpr are varslice groups: one field for all months (time = 0 0 0 0 1) or 12 monthly fields (time = 0 0 0 0 12), on the climate grid or remapped online (remap, grid_src). A group with a time axis (time = 1 x0 x1 dx nsub) is a time-dependent bias: it is sliced at the forcing time at every climate update, as a time-varying snapshot. The weighted annual fields are written to the climate’s 2D file (bias_dtas_ann, bias_fpr_ann; with a time axis also bias_dtas_ann_now, the slice applied).

title: yelmox
text:
Insolation and orbit ([orbit])
The surface models that take the top-of-atmosphere insolation (chion’s ITM and BESSI, smbpal’s ITM) compute it with the insol library (a dependency, libinsol.a), the daily mean in closed form from the orbital elements of Laskar et al. (2004). [orbit] (one per domain, [orbit_north] in yelmox_bipolar) gives the elements; both surface models read it:
&orbit
    method = "fixed_time"   ! forcing_time: at the forcing time time_rel; fixed_time: at time; fixed_orbit: ecc, obl, per
    time   = 0.0            ! [yr] model time of the orbit (fixed_time; relative to 1950, past < 0)
    ecc    = 0.016702       ! [1]   eccentricity (fixed_orbit)
    obl    = 23.4393        ! [deg] obliquity (fixed_orbit)
    per    = 102.918        ! [deg] longitude of perihelion (fixed_orbit)
    fldr   = "input"  ! folder of the orbital tables
/
forcing_time follows the forcing time (ts%time_rel: transient insolation with tstep_method = "rel"); fixed_time holds the orbit of one time (present day by default, the 1950 orbit); fixed_orbit takes the given elements (the defaults are the tables’ at 1950). A fixed orbit is the one exception to the single forcing time. Each model recomputes its insolation only when the elements change, so once per run unless method = "forcing_time". The par files list method and time; the other keys come from input/yelmox_defaults.nml.

title: yelmox
text:
Prescribed ice ([ice_bnd])
Yelmo prescribes the ice thickness in its fixed cells (mask_ice = 1: H_ice = H_ice_ref) and relaxes it towards H_ice_ref in its relaxation cells (tau_relax > 0, with ytopo.topo_rel = -1), set by [yelmo_masks]: a strip at the edge of the region where ice is allowed (border_width = N M: N fixed cells, then M relaxation cells with relax_tau), the expressions mask_ice_fixed and relax, or yelmo.mask_border. [ice_bnd] writes the thickness of an ice history into H_ice_ref in these cells, each step before yelmo_update (step_ice_bnd) and at the cold start; the interior keeps its H_ice_ref (the present-day ice):
file:    H_ice_ref = H_ice(time_rel)        (interpolated; the first or last slice outside the file)
scaled:  H_ice_ref = f * H_ice(slice_time)  (f a series, e.g. before the file starts)
&ice_bnd
    active     = True
    method     = "file"               ! file | scaled
    H_ice      = "paleomist_H_ice"    ! group of the ice thickness [m] (the par file, then [forcing] var_defs)
    index      = ""                   ! scaled: the series f ([forcing] series)
    slice_time = -21e3                ! [yr] scaled: time of the slice
/
input/clim_db.nml holds paleomist_H_ice (PaleoMIST 1.0, 80-0 ka every 2.5 kyr) and glac1d_H_ice (GLAC-1D, 26-0 ka every 100 yr), the IceHistory products on the ice grid. The forcing time is time_rel (a constant-time run holds the ice of tstep_const). At the cold start the isostasy reference is taken before (the present-day ice: the prescribed ice of another time is a load). With a time-varying border use [barysealevel] method = "file": under fastiso the prescribed ice would add to the barystatic sea level. H_ice_ref is written to yelmo.nc. Example: yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml (GRL-PAL, border_width = 2 4, mask_ice_dynamic = "all").

title: yelmox
text:
Configuration
A run is set by these namelist groups. Every key is required (a missing key stops the run), except the keys of an unselected init_method and the [relax] and [opt] groups when their switch in [sim] is off.
The forcing groups have defaults: input/yelmox_defaults.nml declares every key of [forcing], [series_<name>] (template [series]: the tsgen keys, the derived keys, units, restart_every_df), [term_<name>] (template [term]), the snapshot backend ([snapshots], template [snapshot] for [snapshot_<name>]), the climate transforms ([taper], [bias]), the orbit of the insolation ([orbit]), [ice_bnd] and [obm_forcing] (yelmox_bipolar), with the domain suffix of a multi-domain driver ([forcing_north] to [forcing]). A par file lists only what differs; an absent group takes every default (a transform is then inactive). Each read goes through nml_read(..., defaults_file, defaults_group) (the path in libs/yelmox_nml.f90), and a key not declared there stops the run (nml_validate). scripts/check_par_nml.py checks the yelmo groups against input/yelmo_defaults.nml and these groups against input/yelmox_defaults.nml offline (--dead: keys of the other groups that no source reads). The other yelmox groups below are read without defaults.



Group
Sets




[ctrl]
the run: its timeline group, calendar years, the restart bundle to start from


timeline group ([ctrl] run_step)
the timeline: tstep_method, tstep_const, time_init, time_end, dtt


[domain]
the domain: name, physical constants, grid of every component, basin set of the hub (basins) (see Multigrid coupling)


[topo], [regions]
the hub topography; the regions, zones, basins and named masks (masks, mask_<name>)


[comps]
the components: which are active, with which model, how often


[sim]
the conditions of this simulation: cold-start ice state, relaxation, optimization, regional modifications


[relax], [opt]
the parameters of the relaxation and the optimization switched on in [sim]


[output]
the output files; their intervals are [tm_1D], [tm_2D], [tm_2Dsm], and [tm_rst] for restarts



The models have their own groups ([yelmo] and the Yelmo physics groups, [isos], [barysealevel], [marine_shelf], [surface_chion] + [chion], [smbpal], the climate backend’s, …). In yelmox_bipolar the domain groups carry the hemisphere suffix ([domain_north], [comps_north], [sim_north], [relax_north], [opt_north], [output_north], …); [ctrl] and the timeline are shared.
A minimal skeleton:
&ctrl
    run_step        = "ctrl"            ! timeline group ("ctrl" = this group)
    calendar        = False
    calendar_ref    = 1950.0
    restart         = "None"            ! restart bundle folder, or "None" for a cold start
    tstep_method    = "const"
    tstep_const     = 0.0
    time_init       = 0.0
    time_end        = 15e3
    dtt             = 10.0
/

&comps
    with_ice_sheet  = True
    with_isostasy   = True
    with_climate    = True
    with_surface    = True
    with_shelf      = True
    climate         = "snapshots"
    surface_method  = "chion"
    dt_clim         = 10.0
    dt_isos         = 10.0
/

&sim
    init_method       = "none"
    init_marine_H     = False
    init_kill_shelves = False
    init_time_thrm    = 0.0
    relax             = True            ! uses [relax]
    opt               = True            ! uses [opt]
    use_negis         = False
    scale_glacial_smb = False
    lim_pd_ice        = False
/

Forcing library
input/forcing_db.nml holds the named forcing groups that several par files share: snapshots [snapshot_<name>] (PMIP3 picontrol, lgm; the Greenland reconstructions b18_base, b18, b20), series [series_<name>] (glacial, orbital, orbital_t2018, dTo, ramp, hyst, dT, obm_north, obm_south), terms [term_<name>] (glacial, orbital, b18, b20, ocean, ramp, hyst, dT, obm_north, obm_south) and elsa layer settings (elsa_grl_lgp, elsa_grl_deglac, elsa_ant_paleo). [forcing] (the per-run selection), [snapshots] (the backend’s rules) and [snapshot_pd] (domain-specific) stay in the par file.
A named group is read from the par file if it has it, else from the first [forcing] var_defs file that does (default "input/clim_db.nml" "input/forcing_db.nml": the fields, then the library). elsa reads its group from the file [ytrc] elsa_nml names (input/forcing_db.nml), selected by elsa_group. A listed group found nowhere stops the run.
To change a library group for one run, define it in the par file (it wins; LIS and North redefine series_glacial as the constant 1), or set one of its keys with -p (e.g. -p series_glacial.f_min=0): runme copies the whole group into the staged par file, then applies the override (par_library in .runme/info.json). par_defaults (input/yelmo_defaults.nml, input/yelmox_defaults.nml) lets -p set a key of a group the par file lacks, e.g. -p bias.active=True or -p ytrc.use_elsa=True. -p on a library group needs runme 0.5.26 or later.
Scripts follow one rule: the settings that define the experiment go in commented -p arrays (in scripts/<exp>/params.sh when several scripts share them); run control goes in the invocation (run step, times, restart, grid, output intervals, queue).
The forcing builder resolves a base plus -p overrides the same way, draws the forcing the run will see and writes the runme command; scripts/forcing-builder/explain.jl does it on the command line.


[ctrl]








Key
Values





run_step
group name
the group holding the timeline: "ctrl" for [ctrl] itself, or a phase group such as [spinup] or [transient], so one par file can hold several run phases


calendar, calendar_ref
bool, [yr CE]
timeline in calendar years, against the reference year calendar_ref (ESM runs)


restart
folder, "None"
the restart bundle to start from; "None" = cold start



The timeline group holds tstep_method ("const": the time advances and the forcing time stays at tstep_const; "rel": the forcing follows the time, e.g. for paleo records; "cal": calendar time), tstep_const, time_init, time_end and the main time step dtt [yr].
A restart bundle is a folder restart-<kyr>-kyr/, written on the [tm_rst] schedule and always at time_end. It holds one restart file per stateful model, the shared sea level and the transient-forcing state (in yelmox_bipolar also the ocean box model, with each domain in a subfolder named after it). Pass restart as an absolute path: the run starts inside its own folder. A restart continues the run bit for bit: the state is restored, not stepped again (the surface restart files carry the annual fields of the last cycle); only the climate is re-derived from it, which equals the run’s own when the restart time lies on its dt_clim cadence (counted from the start of the run, as are dt_isos and the [relax], [opt] time windows).


[comps]
The components: which are active, with which model, how often.








Key
Values





with_ice_sheet, with_isostasy, with_climate, with_surface, with_shelf
bool
components in the coupling sequence: the ice sheet, isostasy, the climate (atmosphere + ocean), the surface (mass balance + temperature) and the shelf base (melt + temperature); with_surface and with_shelf need with_climate


climate
snapshots, esm, rembo
the climate backend


surface_method
chion (default), smbpal, smb_simple, climate
chion or smbpal (ITM or PDD), both from the climate’s temperature and precipitation; chion runs the ITM, BESSI or PDD snowpack ([chion] model) in daily steps ([surface_chion], [chion]; ITM’s parameters are the group [chion] nml_itm names: smbpal’s [itm], or for Greenland [itm_chion] (alb_ice = 0.31, calibrated to MAR); BESSI gets the surface shortwave as TOA insolation times trans_sw, the TOA insolation itself (chion’s cloud-proxy longwave), the ice thickness, a constant wind_speed and rel_hum, and the air pressure from the surface elevation; its constants are [chion_const], for Greenland alpha_ice = 0.55, calibrated to MAR; BESSI runs pass surface_chion.time_equil=20, converged within 0.3 Gt/yr of the par files’ 100 yr, which ITM needs; PDD’s parameters are the group [chion] nml_pdd names, [pdd_chion] with pdd_method = "cg05" (Calov and Greve, 2005), smbpal’s PDD; the surface temperature of ITM and PDD is chion’s chion_tsrf_annual, the annual-mean air temperature warmed by firn_fac times the annual refreezing, capped at freezing over ice); smb_simple (needs a sea-level air temperature: snapshots); the climate’s own smb (esm, rembo; required by rembo)


dt_clim
[yr]
climate update interval; <= 0: updated only at the cold start


dt_isos
[yr]
isostasy update interval (> 0; 10 in all par files): FastIsostasy integrates the whole interval in one call, the bedrock is held in between





[sim]
The conditions of this simulation: the cold-start ice state (init_*), the relaxation, the optimization and regional modifications. The init_* keys act on a cold start only; relax and opt act on a cold start or a restart, with their times counted from the start of the run (time_init).








Key
Values





init_method
none, equil, recon, recon_ref
cold-start ice state: as initialized; a short equilibration with constant boundaries; the reconstruction recon_path as initial ice where recon_regions selects; the reconstruction as reference ice only


init_equil_time
[yr]
equil: equilibration time


recon_path, recon_var
path, name
recon, recon_ref: the reconstruction file ({domain}, {grid_name} = grid_ice) and its ice-thickness variable


recon_time
yr
recon, recon_ref: model time of the state; the nearest slice of recon_path (its time axis converted from the units: years ago/BP count into the past, kiloyears/ka in thousands)


recon_regions
selection expression
recon: where its ice is imposed (e.g. "region:North_America")


init_marine_H
bool
LGM-like marine ice, before init_method


init_kill_shelves
bool
no ice where the present-day bed is ocean


init_time_thrm
[yr]
then equilibrate with the topography fixed (0 = off)


relax
bool
relax the topography towards the reference ([relax])


opt
bool
optimize the basal friction and the thermal-forcing correction ([opt])


use_negis
bool
NEGIS basal-friction modification ([negis])


scale_glacial_smb
bool
reduce negative glacial smb ([glacial_smb])


lim_pd_ice
bool
extra melt (4 m/yr) outside the present-day ice extent



A spin-up usually sets relax and opt together: the relaxation holds the floating ice and the grounding zone near the observations while the optimization adjusts the basal friction, and then releases them gradually. A run restarted from a spin-up sets both to False to keep the optimized fields fixed.


[relax]

Values

ytopo.topo_rel mode

Future-reference plan for converting the four sibling-directory symlinks in the yelmox root (fesm-utils, FastIsostasy, rembo1, yelmo) into proper git submodules. Not yet executed.


Have yelmox pin specific commits of each component repo and clone them automatically as submodules under the existing paths, replacing the current symlinks to sibling clones under /Users/alrobi001/models/.

URLs: SSH form, matching current remotes. For yelmo use git@github.com:fesmc/yelmo.git (not the palma-ice mirror).
Branch to track: main for all four (default branch on each origin).
.gitmodules form: pin to commit only — no branch = … line. Bumping the pin is an explicit git add <submodule> in yelmox.
Initial pin: tip of origin/main at the time of conversion. Re-fetch and re-check tips before running.
ice_data: untouched.




From the yelmox root:
# 1. Remove symlinks (no data lost — sibling clones at /Users/alrobi001/models/<name> remain)
rm fesm-utils FastIsostasy rembo1 yelmo

# 2. Drop the four entries from .gitignore (paths will now be tracked as submodules)
#    Keep: ice_data, libyelmox, unit_tests, libs/lis*, isostasy_data, etc.

# 3. Add each submodule (clones fresh into yelmox/<path>)
git submodule add git@github.com:fesmc/fesm-utils.git       fesm-utils
git submodule add git@github.com:palma-ice/FastIsostasy.git FastIsostasy
git submodule add git@github.com:alex-robinson/rembo1.git   rembo1
git submodule add git@github.com:fesmc/yelmo.git            yelmo

# 4. Verify .gitmodules + each submodule pin, then single commit:
git commit -m "add submodules: fesm-utils, FastIsostasy, rembo1, yelmo"



Each submodule contributes only its source. The build artifacts the Makefile depends on (fesm-utils/fftw-serial/, fesm-utils/lis-serial/, FastIsostasy/libisostasy/include/, yelmo/libyelmo/include/, rembo1/librembo/include/) are gitignored inside each submodule and must be built per the component’s own install/build process — the same as today.



git config --global push.recurseSubmodules check
So git push in yelmox refuses if any submodule has unpushed commits at its pinned sha. Catches the easy mistake of pushing yelmox with a yelmo pin nobody else can fetch.



cd yelmox/yelmo
git checkout main                   # ALWAYS — fresh clones land in detached HEAD
# edit, build via yelmox Makefile, iterate
git commit -am "..."
git push                            # to fesmc/yelmo

cd ..                               # back to yelmox root
git status                          # shows: modified: yelmo (new commits)
git add yelmo                       # bump the pin
git commit -m "bump yelmo to <sha>: <reason>"
After a fresh git clone --recurse-submodules of yelmox elsewhere, put all submodules on their branches in one shot:
git submodule foreach 'git checkout main || git checkout master'


If a yelmox change needs a matching yelmo change: push the yelmo branch first, then in yelmox commit the gitlink bump together with the yelmox-side code that uses the new API — that single yelmox commit becomes the atomic unit. push.recurseSubmodules = check enforces the ordering.



After conversion there are two clones of (e.g.) yelmo on disk: the original at /Users/alrobi001/models/yelmo and the submodule at /Users/alrobi001/models/yelmox/yelmo. They drift unless synced via the remote. Three options at conversion time:

(a) Abandon the siblings; develop only inside the submodule. Simplest mental model.
(b) Keep the siblings as the primary workspace; push from sibling and git pull inside the submodule. Two extra commands per sync but reuses one dev tree across multiple yelmox checkouts/worktrees.
(c) Point the submodule at the sibling locally with git config submodule.<name>.url /Users/alrobi001/models/<name> (then git submodule sync). Submodule fetches from the local path; .gitmodules still points at GitHub for everyone else. Useful for one-yelmo-feeds-many-yelmox setups.

After conversion, the fesm-utils + FastIsostasy alex-dev branches still exist and are ahead of/behind main in various ways — decide separately whether to retire those branches or keep them as long-lived dev lines.

title: Multigrid coupling
text:
Architecture of the two YelmoX programs, yelmox and yelmox_bipolar. Each component of a domain (Yelmo, isostasy, climate, smb, marine shelf) runs on its own grid, and fields are remapped between grids at the moment of coupling. The domain is defined around a hi-resolution geometry hub (htopo), the finest grid of the setup, from which every component, Yelmo included, is populated.
Example for Antarctica with Yelmo on ANT-16KM and a hi-res hub on ANT-2KM:

H_ice (Yelmo ANT-16KM) → bilin → ANT-2KM for the marine-shelf calc.
z_bed/z_ss from FastIsostasy → conservatively aggregated to Yelmo’s grid, set as BCs.
marine_shelf computed at ANT-2KM; bmb_shlf/T_shlf → conservatively aggregated → ANT-16KM → passed to Yelmo as forcing.

The bookkeeping of the remapping steps lives in a coupler (fesm-utils) and in the domain’s coupling steps (yelmox), not in the component modules.



Component modules are grid-agnostic. marshelf_update, isos_update, snapshots_update, smbpal_update all take/return plain (nx,ny) arrays; the grid is the caller’s choice. Moving a module onto another grid is a caller-side change, not a module change.
map_class self-identifies and self-caches. It stores name1, name2, method, and map_init loads from / saves to a maps/ folder on disk. A map object already carries its own identity key; disk caching across runs is free.
method is baked into the map at map_init time ("con" = area weights, "bilin" = neighbor weights). So method is part of the map cache key. stat (mean/count/stdev) is applied at map_field time and does not change the map — it is a per-call pass-through, not a key.
map_field is generic over kind. The interface already covers dp, sp (map_field_grid_grid_sp) and int (map_field_grid_grid_int); the sp/int variants accumulate in dp internally. So remap never converts precision outside — it calls the generic map_field and lets it dispatch by kind.




Grids are nodes; maps are directed, method-typed edges. 16KM→2KM bilin (downscale) and 2KM→16KM con (aggregate) are two distinct objects even between the same pair. Worst case is N·(N−1)·methods edges, but a real run uses a handful. Maps are built lazily (only edges actually used) and each is built once, stored once, and shared — the only hard requirement, because a hi-res target map is both expensive to build and large in memory.



fesm-utils/src/coupler.f90        coupler_class + remap (grids, map cache)
        │
        ▼
yelmox/libs/
  kryos.f90             kryos_domain, domain_ctl, domain_init, remap
  kryos_coupling.f90    step_* and couple_* primitives
  kryos_startup.f90     cold start, restart bundles (domain_startup, ...)
  kryos_output.f90      per-module 2D/1D output, CMIP output
  kryos_regions.f90     named regions, marine-ice start, NEGIS, glacial smb
  kryos_forcing.f90     driver-owned series registry (tsgen, derived)
  yelmox_climate.f90    climate backends behind one interface (climate_out)
  climate_terms.f90     the terms of the forcing (series x pattern) on the climate
  climate_mods.f90      climate transforms after the terms (taper, bias)
        │
        ▼
yelmox/yelmox.f90                 single domain
yelmox_bipolar/yelmox_bipolar.f90 north + south, shared sea level + OBM
Dependency flow is one-directional. The coupler is pure grid/map machinery and knows nothing about yelmox. The Kryos modules know the physics modules but no driver, so both programs share them.



call coupler_init(cpl, map_fldr, gen)               ! map folder, default map generator
call coupler_add_grid(cpl, name, grid)              ! optional in-memory grid
call coupler_prime(cpl, src, dst, method, gen)      ! build a map up front
call remap(cpl, var_src, src, var_dst, dst, method, stat)
Grids are identified by string name in every remap call. A name resolves to its grid definition from disk by default — grid_<name>.txt in the map folder (maps/), read via grid_cdo_read_desc (both the fesm-utils # header and cdo-native CF projection keys). coupler_add_grid registers an in-memory grid that wins over the disk definition. Nothing is hardcoded: the available grids are the grid_*.txt files in maps/.
remap finds the map for (src, dst, method) in the cache, or builds it (from its disk cache when present) and stores it. method is "con" (conservative, the default) or a distance kernel ("nn", "shepard", "quadrant", "bilin"); stat (mean/count/stdev) is forwarded per call. gen ("coords", the default, or "cdo") only selects how the weights are built. remap covers dp/sp/int × 2D/3D, and sizes the destination itself. The maps live in fixed-capacity storage, so adding a map never deep-copies the (large) maps already built.
The domain wraps it as remap(dom, var_src, src, var_dst, dst, method) (kryos), which copies when src == dst, so a component on Yelmo’s grid costs nothing.



The whole state of one region is bundled into kryos_domain:
type kryos_domain
    type(yelmo_class)          :: yelmo
    type(marshelf_class)       :: mshlf
    type(isos_class)           :: isos
    type(yelmox_climate_class) :: cl     ! climate backend ([comps] climate)
    type(climate_out_class)    :: clim   ! backend-agnostic climate output (now/ref)
    type(smbpal_class)         :: smb
    type(smb_simple_class)     :: smbs   ! surface_method = "smb_simple"
    type(sediments_class)      :: sed
    type(geothermal_class)     :: gthrm
    type(phys_const_class)     :: cnst   ! physical constants, shared by every component
    type(htopo_class)          :: topo   ! hi-res geometry hub
    type(coupler_class)        :: cpl    ! this region's grids + map cache
    type(ice_opt_params)       :: opt    ! spin-up optimization
    type(negis_params)         :: ngs
    type(glacial_smb_params)   :: gsmb
    type(domain_ctl)           :: ctl    ! [domain], [comps], [sim], [output]
end type
The barystatic sea level (bsl) and the transient forcing (tsf) are not part of the domain: they are driver-owned, so a multi-domain driver shares them (or not). Each step_* primitive advances one component on its own grid and is a no-op when that component is inactive (with_*); each couple_*_to_yelmo lands one component’s output on Yelmo’s grid. Two domains (bipolar) carry their own coupler and grids, so they never collide.
The climate reaches the rest of the domain only through climate_out_class (now and ref): the atmosphere, the ocean as depth profiles or at the shelf base, and, when the backend has them, the surface mass balance and subglacial discharge. Nothing downstream depends on which backend produced them.


One [domain] group ([domain_north]/[domain_south] in bipolar) defines the domain: its name, its physical constants and the grid of every component. Its topography is in [topo] and its regions, zones and basins in [regions] ([topo_south], [regions_south], … in bipolar), all from FesmData v2 (fesmdata/). Yelmo takes the domain name and its grid from [domain] ([yelmo] no longer sets domain/grid_name). A blank component grid takes its default:
&domain
    name         = "Antarctica"
    phys_const   = "Earth"      ! physical constants: group of input/yelmo_phys_const.nml
    grid_hub     = "ANT-16KM"   ! hi-res geometry hub
    grid_ice     = "ANT-32KM"   ! Yelmo                                [grid_hub]
    grid_isos    = ""           ! isostasy                             [grid_ice]
    grid_clim    = ""           ! reference climate + transient forcing [grid_ice]
    grid_surface = ""           ! surface mass balance                 [grid_clim]
    grid_shelf   = ""           ! marine shelf                         [grid_hub]
    basins       = "Zwally2012" ! basin ids of the hub output
/
&topo
    path  = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc"
    vars  = "z_bed" "z_srf" "H_ice" "z_bed_sd"
    remap = "con"
/
&regions
    path_regions = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_REGIONS.nc"
    path_basins  = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_BASINS-{set}.nc"
    basin_sets   = "Zwally2012"
    masks        = "APIS" "WAIS" "EAIS"           ! named regions for 1D output
    mask_APIS    = "region:Antarctic_Peninsula"
    mask_WAIS    = "region:West_Antarctica"
    mask_EAIS    = "region:East_Antarctica"
/
{domain}/{grid_name} in the paths resolve to name/grid_hub. The groups are those of fesm-utils topodata and regions (see the fesm-utils docs), which also describe the selection expressions used below ("region:Greenland & ~zone:open_ocean") and layers of other files (layers, path_<layer>, var_<layer>, e.g. the ISMIP7 basins).
The other inputs are FesmData v2 products as well (fesmdata/, the link to $FESMDATA that runme copies into each run folder), on the grid of the component that reads them. The geothermal heat flux ([ghf]) and the sediments ([sed]) are remapped (bilinear) onto the Yelmo grid when their file is on another grid (its global attribute grid_name), so obs_path may name a coarser grid, e.g. fesmdata/{domain}/PYR-2KM/PYR-2KM_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc on PYR-250M.
The domain loads its physical constants once (phys_const_load, the group phys_const of input/yelmo_phys_const.nml) and hands the same record to every component: the hub, Yelmo (yelmo_init cnst), isostasy, the marine shelf and smb_simple. Yelmo’s own yelmo.phys_const then only selects its calendar year (sec_year).
htopo (fesm-utils) holds the hub. It sits above every physics module (including Yelmo): its grid (grid_hub) is the finest resolution in the setup, and it is the reference geometry the coupler remaps from. On the hub grid it holds the reference topography (topo%ref: z_bed, H_ice, z_srf, z_bed_sd), the regions (topo%reg) and the current geometry z_bed/H_ice/z_srf/f_grnd/z_sl (refreshed each step, see below). htopo_init resolves the grid from grid_<name>.txt (the disk grid table). Gaps in the topography (missing values, e.g. outside the coverage of the source dataset) are filled: no ice, the bed from the nearest valid cell, the surface from the bed and the ice thickness (sea level 0).
Yelmo is populated from the domain like the other components. Its grid comes from maps/grid_<grid_ice>.txt (yelmo_init_grid, grid_def="none"), and the hub’s z_bed/H_ice/z_srf/z_bed_sd, remapped conservatively to grid_ice, are both its initial topography and its present-day reference (yelmo_init topo_init/topo_pd). Yelmo then processes them as it would its own files ([yelmo_init_topo] keeps init_topo_state, z_bed_f_sd, smoothing; its grad_lim_zb applies). Where grid_ice = grid_hub the remap is a copy.
The hub follows the models each step (couple_yelmo_to_htopo, after Yelmo). On Yelmo’s grid it mirrors Yelmo, fractional grounding included. On a finer hub it keeps its hi-res reference and adds Yelmo’s anomalies, refined bilinearly: the bed displacement z_bed - z_bed_ref, and the change in ice thickness from the hub reference as Yelmo received it (remapped conservatively), clipped at zero thickness. htopo_update then recomputes on the hub the grounding (0 or 1, from flotation) and the surface elevation, with Yelmo’s densities; sea level is refined bilinearly. The hi-res bed and ice therefore reach the marine shelf and the climate’s surface elevation, instead of a refined copy of Yelmo’s fields.
The regions reach every component on its own grid (the files of the hub grid, nearest neighbour), and each component makes its own masks from them once at init, with selection expressions in its own group:

Yelmo ([yelmo_masks], yelmo_init reg): where ice is dynamic or fixed (mask_ice_dynamic, mask_ice_fixed; Yelmo’s mask_border then sets the domain border), where it relaxes to the reference (relax, relax_tau, with ytopo.topo_rel = -1), the region of the error metrics (mask_rmse), its basins (basins), and the named regions of [regions] with their own 1D output, yelmo_ts_<name>.nc.
The marine shelf ([marine_shelf]): the reference ocean mask (mask_ocean, mask_deep_ocean), PICO’s margin (mask_pico_deep), its basins (basins) and the corrections by region (corr_method = none | tf | bmb, corr_names, corr_values and one expression corr_<name> per name).
The climate ([esm] basins): the basins of the ocean extrapolation.
The domain: where a reconstruction’s ice is imposed ([sim] recon_regions) and the NEGIS parts ([negis] region_centre/south/north).

A basin spec is "<set>", "<set>.group" (e.g. "Zwally2012.group", the Greenland major systems), "None" (no basins) or "domain" (the whole domain is one basin).



Fields that cross a grid boundary land in step-local allocatables, not a coupler-owned pool. remap takes the destination as intent(inout), allocatable and sizes it itself (allocate-on-demand, reshape if wrong), so callers never hand-compute nx,ny. title: Multigrid coupling
text:
Component modules are grid-agnostic. marshelf_update, isos_update, snapshots_update, smbpal_update all take/return plain (nx,ny) arrays; the grid is the caller’s choice. Moving a module onto another grid is a caller-side change, not a module change.
map_class self-identifies and self-caches. It stores name1, name2, method, and map_init loads from / saves to a maps/ folder on disk. A map object already carries its own identity key; disk caching across runs is free.
method is baked into the map at map_init time ("con" = area weights, "bilin" = neighbor weights). So method is part of the map cache key. stat (mean/count/stdev) is applied at map_field time and does not change the map — it is a per-call pass-through, not a key.
map_field is generic over kind. The interface already covers dp, sp (map_field_grid_grid_sp) and int (map_field_grid_grid_int); the sp/int variants accumulate in dp internally. So remap never converts precision outside — it calls the generic map_field and lets it dispatch by kind.

title: Multigrid coupling
text: Grids are nodes; maps are directed, method-typed edges. 16KM→2KM bilin (downscale) and 2KM→16KM con (aggregate) are two distinct objects even between the same pair. Worst case is N·(N−1)·methods edges, but a real run uses a handful. Maps are built lazily (only edges actually used) and each is built once, stored once, and shared — the only hard requirement, because a hi-res target map is both expensive to build and large in memory.

text:

title: Multigrid coupling
text:
call coupler_init(cpl, map_fldr, gen)               ! map folder, default map generator
call coupler_add_grid(cpl, name, grid)              ! optional in-memory grid
call coupler_prime(cpl, src, dst, method, gen)      ! build a map up front
call remap(cpl, var_src, src, var_dst, dst, method, stat)
Grids are identified by string name in every remap call. A name resolves to its grid definition from disk by default — grid_<name>.txt in the map folder (maps/), read via grid_cdo_read_desc (both the fesm-utils # header and cdo-native CF projection keys). coupler_add_grid registers an in-memory grid that wins over the disk definition. Nothing is hardcoded: the available grids are the grid_*.txt files in maps/.
remap finds the map for (src, dst, method) in the cache, or builds it (from its disk cache when present) and stores it. method is "con" (conservative, the default) or a distance kernel ("nn", "shepard", "quadrant", "bilin"); stat (mean/count/stdev) is forwarded per call. gen ("coords", the default, or "cdo") only selects how the weights are built. remap covers dp/sp/int × 2D/3D, and sizes the destination itself. The maps live in fixed-capacity storage, so adding a map never deep-copies the (large) maps already built.
The domain wraps it as remap(dom, var_src, src, var_dst, dst, method) (kryos), which copies when src == dst, so a component on Yelmo’s grid costs nothing.

type kryos_domain
    type(yelmo_class)          :: yelmo
    type(marshelf_class)       :: mshlf
    type(isos_class)           :: isos
    type(yelmox_climate_class) :: cl     ! climate backend ([comps] climate)
    type(climate_out_class)    :: clim   ! backend-agnostic climate output (now/ref)
    type(smbpal_class)         :: smb
    type(smb_simple_class)     :: smbs   ! surface_method = "smb_simple"
    type(sediments_class)      :: sed
    type(geothermal_class)     :: gthrm
    type(phys_const_class)     :: cnst   ! physical constants, shared by every component
    type(htopo_class)          :: topo   ! hi-res geometry hub
    type(coupler_class)        :: cpl    ! this region's grids + map cache
    type(ice_opt_params)       :: opt    ! spin-up optimization

    type(glacial_smb_params)   :: gsmb

end type
The barystatic sea level (bsl) and the transient forcing (tsf) are not part of the domain: they are driver-owned, so a multi-domain driver shares them (or not). The climate reaches the rest of the domain only through climate_out_class (now and ref): the atmosphere, the ocean as depth profiles or at the shelf base, and, when the backend has them, the surface mass balance and subglacial discharge. Nothing downstream depends on which backend produced them.


One [domain] group ([domain_north]/[domain_south] in bipolar) defines the domain: its name, its physical constants and the grid of every component. &domain
    name         = "Antarctica"
    phys_const   = "Earth"      ! physical constants: group of input/yelmo_phys_const.nml
    grid_hub     = "ANT-16KM"   ! hi-res geometry hub
    grid_ice     = "ANT-32KM"   ! Yelmo                                [grid_hub]
    grid_isos    = ""           ! isostasy                             [grid_ice]
    grid_clim    = ""           ! reference climate + transient forcing [grid_ice]
    grid_surface = ""           ! surface mass balance                 [grid_clim]
    grid_shelf   = ""           ! marine shelf                         [grid_hub]
    basins       = "Zwally2012" ! basin ids of the hub output
/
&topo
    path  = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc"
    vars  = "z_bed" "z_srf" "H_ice" "z_bed_sd"
    remap = "con"
/
&regions
    path_regions = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_REGIONS.nc"
    path_basins  = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_BASINS-{set}.nc"
    basin_sets   = "Zwally2012"
    masks        = "APIS" "WAIS" "EAIS"           ! named regions for 1D output
    mask_APIS    = "region:Antarctic_Peninsula"
    mask_WAIS    = "region:West_Antarctica"
    mask_EAIS    = "region:East_Antarctica"
/

The other inputs are FesmData v2 products as well (fesmdata/, the link to $FESMDATA that runme copies into each run folder), on the grid of the component that reads them. The domain loads its physical constants once (phys_const_load, the group phys_const of input/yelmo_phys_const.nml) and hands the same record to every component: the hub, Yelmo (yelmo_init cnst), isostasy, the marine shelf and smb_simple. Yelmo’s own yelmo.phys_const then only selects its calendar year (sec_year).
htopo (fesm-utils) holds the hub. It sits above every physics module (including Yelmo): its grid (grid_hub) is the finest resolution in the setup, and it is the reference geometry the coupler remaps from. Yelmo is populated from the domain like the other components. Yelmo then processes them as it would its own files ([yelmo_init_topo] keeps init_topo_state, z_bed_f_sd, smoothing; its grad_lim_zb applies). Where grid_ice = grid_hub the remap is a copy.
The hub follows the models each step (couple_yelmo_to_htopo, after Yelmo). On Yelmo’s grid it mirrors Yelmo, fractional grounding included. On a finer hub it keeps its hi-res reference and adds Yelmo’s anomalies, refined bilinearly: the bed displacement z_bed - z_bed_ref, and the change in ice thickness from the hub reference as Yelmo received it (remapped conservatively), clipped at zero thickness. htopo_update then recomputes on the hub the grounding (0 or 1, from flotation) and the surface elevation, with Yelmo’s densities; sea level is refined bilinearly. The climate ([esm] basins): the basins of the ocean extrapolation.
The domain: where a reconstruction’s ice is imposed ([sim] recon_regions) and the NEGIS parts ([negis] region_centre/south/north).

title: Forcing builder
text:
Choose a base par file, change the run control and the forcing, and read off what the run will impose: the forcing time, each series on the run’s timeline, the terms and their anomalies, the sea level, with the equations behind them and the values they take. The result is the runme command, with the -p overrides that reproduce the choices, to copy into a script.
How it is built: a run’s configuration is its base par file (yelmox/yelmox_<domain>.nml) plus -p overrides, resolved against the forcing library (input/forcing_db.nml) and the schema defaults (input/yelmox_defaults.nml), see yelmox. The page reads those files as exported to forcing-builder/forcing.json by scripts/forcing-builder/export.jl; it has no server. Every widget is one namelist key, labelled with where its value comes from (base, library, default, override). The series curves follow the fesm-utils tsgen formulas; scripts/forcing-builder/explain.jl prints the same resolution and draws the same figures on the command line, for a par file with -p options or an existing run folder.
Limits: scalar series only (the 2D snapshot fields are listed, not drawn; a derived series, set by the model, is shown by its definition); single-domain yelmox groups (no domain suffix); the -p list is a fixed override per key, not an ensemble.

text: Two mountain-glacier domains with the ice sheet at 250 m and no ocean ([comps] with_shelf = False): the Pyrenees over the last glacial cycle, -120 kyr to the present, forced by a spatially homogeneous air-temperature anomaly from an orbital index, and SRG (basin set SanRafael), 200 yr in the present-day climate.

title: Mountain glaciers
text:
Running

Climate: snapshots on an orbital index
The reference pd plus the term orbital ([term_orbital], picontrol -> lgm on tas and pr): the temperature adds the PMIP3 LGM – piControl anomaly scaled by the series orbital, the precipitation is multiplied by their ratio. The PMIP3 snapshots give the annual mean and JJA temperature (monthly = False) and the annual precipitation, smoothed over 50 km at loading (clim_sigma = 50). title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
Most forcing in YelmoX is now loaded through the shared varslice reader. A database namelist is a small, static description of a dataset on disk: where the file lives, which variable to read, how to convert its units, and how its records map onto a time axis. The consuming modules — varslice itself, esm_forcing, snapshots, ismip6 — all read the same group layout, so once you understand one group you understand them all.
The point of these files is to keep the provenance of every forcing field visible and in one place. Nothing in the namelist runs code; each group is a declarative record that says “this NetCDF file, this variable, these units, this period” — everything the reader needs to ingest the dataset and hand back a time-indexed field.
See input/esm/esm_ant_ismip7.nml for a full, real-world example.

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
Anatomy of a group
A single dataset is described by one namelist group. All five keys are mandatory (the reader pre-sets defaults, but the convention is to always write them out so the provenance stays in the file):
&gcm_ts_ref
    filename    = "ice_data/{domain}/{grid_name}/RACMO2.3/{grid_name}_ERA5-3H_RACMO2.3p2_1979-2022_monthly.nc"
    name        = "t2m"
    units       = "K" "K"
    scaling     = 1.0 0.0
    time        = 1, 1979.0, 2022.0, 1.0, 12.0
/



Key
Type
Meaning




filename
string
Path to the NetCDF file (relative to the run dir). May contain placeholders and wildcards — see Paths.


name
string
Name of the variable to read inside the NetCDF file.


units
2 strings
"<units_in>" "<units_out>" — documentation labels only.


scaling
2 reals
<unit_scale> <unit_offset> — the actual linear unit conversion.


time
5 reals
<active> <x0> <x1> <dx> <sub> — describes the time axis. See The time array.



The group name (&gcm_ts_ref, &gcm_to_proj, …) is chosen by the consuming module — it decides which physical role a group plays (reference vs. projection, atmosphere vs. ocean, etc.). The five keys inside are always the same.

units vs. scaling
The two units strings are labels for humans — they do not trigger any conversion. The real conversion is the linear transform in scaling, applied to every value as it is read:
value_out = value_in * unit_scale + unit_offset
units documents the intent so a reader can check that scaling actually performs it. For example, precipitation stored in kg m-2 s-1 and wanted in mm yr-1:
units   = "kg m-2 s-1" "mm yr-1"
scaling = 31556926.25 0.0     ! CMIP standard seconds-per-year
or ocean temperature stored in °C and wanted in K:
units   = "degrees C" "K"
scaling = 1.0 273.15
Use scaling = 1.0 0.0 when no conversion is needed.

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
The time array
The time key is the only subtle one. It packs five numbers:
time = active, x0, x1, dx, sub








Element
Name
Meaning




active
with_time
1 = the field is time-varying (read record-by-record). 0 = the field is static (one slice); x0..x1 then merely document the period the data represents.


x0
start
First time value on the axis (calendar year, in ESM convention).


x1
end
Last time value on the axis.


dx
step
Spacing between successive major time units (usually 1.0 year).


sub
sub-count
Number of sub-annual records per major unit: 1 = annual, 12 = monthly. Any value > 1 switches on sub-annual handling.



How the reader interprets these:

Static field (active = 0). x0..x1 are preserved as-is and describe the period the (single) slice represents. Typical for a fixed surface elevation or an ocean climatology:
time = 0, 2000, 2000, 0, 1     ! one slice, "representing year 2000"
time = 0, 1990, 2014, 0, 1     ! one slice, "a 1990–2014 climatology"
Time-varying, annual (active = 1, sub = 1). The axis is built as x0, x0+dx, …, x1:
time = 1, 1850, 2014, 1, 1     ! 165 annual records, 1850…2014
Time-varying, sub-annual (active = 1, sub > 1). A sub-annual axis is built with spacing 1/sub, centred within each major unit (e.g. mid-month for sub = 12), spanning x0 through x1:
time = 1, 1979.0, 2022.0, 1.0, 12.0   ! monthly records, Jan 1979 … Dec 2022
Static field, sub-annual (active = 0, sub > 1). active and sub are independent switches: active decides whether the field advances along a multi-year calendar axis, sub decides whether there is a within-year (monthly) cycle. Combining them gives a monthly climatology — a fixed seasonal cycle, selected by month-of-year, that does not advance year to year. x0..x1 document the period the climatology averages over; dx = 0:
time = 0, 1961, 1990, 0, 12     ! 12-month climatology, averaged over 1961–1990
The last dimension of the variable is the cycle: t2m(x,y,month) or, with depth, to(x,y,depth,month). An update with method = "range_mean" and rep = 1 gives its mean over the cycle (e.g. the annual-mean reference ocean of esm_forcing); any other update keeps the cycle.
Collapse to a single slice. For a time-varying field, setting dx = 0 collapses x1 to x0, i.e. read exactly one record at x0. (For a static field, dx = 0 is normal and x0..x1 are left untouched.)

The generated axis length must match the length of the NetCDF file’s time dimension, or the reader stops with an error — a useful check that x0, x1, dx, sub describe the file you actually pointed at.

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
Paths: placeholders and wildcards
filename is expanded before the file is opened.
Placeholders in {braces} are substituted by the caller:

{domain} and {grid_name} are built in — every module supplies them (e.g. Antarctica, ANT-16KM).
Additional keys are passed by the consuming module. esm_forcing, for instance, supplies {gcm} and {experiment}, so an ISMIP7 projection path can read:
filename = "ice_data/ISMIP7/{domain}/{grid_name}/{gcm}/{experiment}/ocean/thetao/v3/{grid_name}_{gcm}_{experiment}_v3_2015-2299_thetao.nc"
and the same namelist serves every GCM/experiment combination — you select the concrete values in the driver’s [esm] configuration, not here. snapshots supplies {grid_global} ([snapshots] grid_global) and {exp} (the snapshot’s exp) for its database input/clim_db.nml (see Snapshots).

Wildcards (shell globs, * and ?) are also allowed. The reader expands the pattern with ls -1 … | sort, so a dataset split across many files is matched and concatenated in alphabetical order:
filename = "ice_data/{domain}/{grid_name}/{gcm}/historical/tas/*.nc"
Sort the split so alphabetical order equals chronological order (zero-pad years).

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
Worked examples
Monthly, time-varying reference climate (RACMO2.3 on the ice grid):
&gcm_ts_ref
    filename    = "ice_data/{domain}/{grid_name}/RACMO2.3/{grid_name}_ERA5-3H_RACMO2.3p2_1979-2022_monthly.nc"
    name        = "t2m"
    units       = "K" "K"
    scaling     = 1.0 0.0
    time        = 1, 1979.0, 2022.0, 1.0, 12.0
/
Annual ESM projection ocean temperature, °C → K, GCM/experiment templated:
&gcm_to_proj
    filename    = "ice_data/ISMIP7/{domain}/{grid_name}/{gcm}/{experiment}/ocean/thetao/v3/{grid_name}_{gcm}_{experiment}_v3_2015-2299_thetao.nc"
    name        = "thetao"
    units       = "degrees C" "K"
    scaling     = 1.0 273.15
    time        = 1, 2015, 2299, 1, 1
/
Static surface elevation (single slice, no unit change):
&gcm_zs_ref
    filename    = "fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_SMB-RACMO2.3p2-1985-2014.nc"
    name        = "z_srf"
    units       = "m" "m"
    scaling     = 1.0 0.0
    time        = 0, 2000, 2000, 0, 1
/
Static ocean climatology (single slice representing a 1990–2014 average):
&gcm_to_ref
    filename    = "ice_data/ISMIP7/{domain}/{grid_name}/meltMIP/{grid_name}_OI_Climatology_thetao_extrap.nc"
    name        = "thetao"
    units       = "degrees C" "K"
    scaling     = 1.0 273.15
    time        = 0, 1990, 2014, 0, 1
/

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
How the groups are consumed
A module loads a group into a varslice object once at initialization (varslice_init_nml(vs, filename, group, domain, grid_name, subs=…)) and then asks for a field at a given time during the run (varslice_update(vs, time, method=…)). The database namelist supplies everything the object needs; the method (e.g. exact, interp, extrap) is chosen by the caller at read time, not in the namelist.

esm_forcing groups the atmosphere/ocean database groups into reference, variability, ESM-reference, historical, and projection periods (&gcm_ts_ref, &gcm_to_proj, …) and supplies {gcm}/{experiment}. See ESM forcing.
snapshots uses the same reader for its snapshot climate database.
ismip6 uses it for the ISMIP6 atmosphere/ocean forcing files.

Because they share the reader, the layout documented here is identical across all of them — a group is a group regardless of which module owns it.

title: Database namelists (varslice)
text:
Quick reference

All five keys are mandatory; always write them for provenance.
Optional: fill ("none", "nearest": each level from the nearest valid cell, a level without data from the level above, or "const" with fill_value), and remap (kernel) with grid_src (the file’s grid) to read a field on another grid.
units = two documentation labels; scaling = [scale, offset] does the real out = in*scale + offset conversion.
time = [active, x0, x1, dx, sub]: active 1/0 = time-varying/static · sub 1/12 = annual/monthly · dx = 0 collapses a time-varying field to a single slice at x0.
Paths expand {domain}/{grid_name} plus module-supplied keys like {gcm}/{experiment}, and accept */? globs (sorted alphabetically).
The generated time axis length must match the file’s time dimension.

title: Snapshots
text:
The snapshot backend snapshots builds the climate from a reference snapshot (e.g. present day) plus the terms of [forcing]: each a scalar series on the forcing time (e.g. a glacial index) times a pattern, the difference of two snapshots (e.g. LGM minus pre-industrial) or a uniform anomaly (see yelmox), on the fesm-utils varslice reader and tsgen series. It supplies the atmosphere (monthly tas, pr, lapse-rate corrected to the current surface) and the ocean as depth profiles (to_ann, so_ann), which the marine shelf interpolates to the shelf base. It runs on grid_clim, reads [snapshots] and the [snapshot_<name>] groups, and also supplies the ocean of the rembo climate (an ocean-only reference snapshot).
The transforms [taper] and [bias] (see yelmox) apply after the terms, in this order.

title: Snapshots
text:
Configuration
Example: yelmox/yelmox_Greenland.nml, present day plus the PMIP3 LGM minus piControl anomaly weighted by the orbital index, the ocean plus a quarter of the mean air temperature anomaly (the derived series dTo):
&forcing
    reference = "pd"                  ! [snapshot_pd], in the par file
    series    = "orbital" "dTo"       ! [series_orbital], [series_dTo] (library)
    terms     = "orbital" "ocean"     ! [term_orbital]: picontrol -> lgm on tas, pr; [term_ocean]: dTo on to
/

&snapshots
    lapse     = 0.0080 0.0065         ! [K m-1] annual, summer (default)
    f_p       = 0.06                  ! [K-1] precipitation scaling (default 0.05)
/
The snapshots of the run are the reference and the snap0/snap1 of its terms (no list): pd, picontrol and lgm here. Every key of [snapshots] and [snapshot_<name>] has a default in input/yelmox_defaults.nml (see Defaults): combine = "anomaly" (snapshots as anomalies from the reference), fields = "tas" "pr" "to" "so" "zs" (the fields a snapshot may bind), grid_global = "GLOBAL-1DEG", … Two kinds of group:

Rules, [snapshots]: the lapse rates lapse (annual, summer) and the precipitation sensitivity f_p (β_p), used in the sea-level reduction of the snapshots, the uniform terms and the move to the model surface.
Snapshots, [snapshot_<name>]: exp (the experiment, {exp} in the database paths), monthly (default True), clim_sigma/ocn_sigma ([km] Gaussian smoothing of the atmosphere and the ocean at loading, the land mask following the smoothed elevation; default 0), tas_season and, per field, the database group(s) holding it (see Database).


Database
The snapshots bind varslice groups (see Database namelists) by name, from the par file itself if it has the group (searched implicitly first, so it never has to name itself and its groups win), else from the files listed in [forcing] var_defs, searched in order (first file that has the group). The snapshot groups [snapshot_<name>], the series and the terms are looked up the same way. The shared database input/clim_db.nml holds one group per product field; a par file can add run-specific groups:
&forcing
    var_defs = "input/clim_db.nml" "input/forcing_db.nml"   ! the default
/
&my_tas                              ! in the par file: found before clim_db.nml
    filename = "ice_data/..."
    ...
/
A group missing from the par file and every var_defs file stops the run, naming the group and the files. The paths of the database take, besides {domain} and {grid_name}, two keywords:

{grid_global}: the global grid of the paleoclimate products, [snapshots] grid_global (default GLOBAL-1DEG);
{exp}: the experiment of the snapshot, its exp, so one group serves every experiment of a product family.

Present-day references are regional ({domain}/{grid_name}, the resolution of the climate grid): MAR v3.14 1961-1990 (mar314_1961_1990_{tas,sf,rf,pr,zs}), RACMO2.3p2 1981-2010 (racmo23p2_1981_2010_{tas,tsrf,pr,sf,zs}), ERA5 1981-2010 (era5_1981_2010_{tas,pr,sf,zs}), ORAS5 1981-2010 (oras5_1981_2010_{to,so}, monthly climatology) and the ISMIP7 ocean (ismip7_{to,so}). The paleoclimate snapshots are the global products, remapped online onto the climate grid (remap = "bilin", the map cached in maps/):

{exp}

The Greenland reconstructions are regional products on GRL-16KM, remapped online (grid_src = "GRL-16KM") and filled from the nearest cell outside their box (fill = "nearest", e.g. on GRL-PAL):
