The database also holds the groups of the transforms ([bias]: bias_mar_era5_1981_2010_{dtas,fpr}; [taper]: taper_b18_b20) and the ice histories of [ice_bnd] (paleomist_H_ice, glac1d_H_ice).
Time-varying groups. A group with a time axis (time = 1 x0 x1 dx nsub) is sliced at the forcing time time_rel at the start and at every climate update: linear interpolation between the two bracketing records, the first or last record outside the axis (varslice extrap). Its snapshot is then reduced to sea level again (and the reference reset, if it is the reference). A group without a time axis (time = 0 ...) is read once at the start.
&snapshot_pd
    tas = "mar314_1961_1990_tas"
    pr  = "mar314_1961_1990_sf" "mar314_1961_1990_rf"
    zs  = "mar314_1961_1990_zs"
    to  = "oras5_1981_2010_to"
    so  = "oras5_1981_2010_so"
/

&snapshot_lgm
    exp        = "lgm"
    monthly    = False
    clim_sigma = 50.0
    tas = "pmip3_mean_tas_ann" "pmip3_mean_tas_jja"
    pr  = "pmip3_mean_pr_ann"
    zs  = "pmip3_mean_zs"
/


Defaults
input/yelmox_defaults.nml declares every key of [snapshots] and [snapshot_<name>], of the forcing ([forcing], the series, the terms) and of the transforms, with its default. The named groups fall back to a template group: [snapshot_<name>] to [snapshot], [snapshots<sfx>] to [snapshots] with the domain suffix of a multi-domain driver ([snapshots_north]). A par file lists only what differs; a key the defaults file does not declare stops the run (nml_validate), and scripts/check_par_nml.py reports it offline.


Fields and composition
Fields are optional per snapshot. A snapshot binds the fields it names (a key absent or "" binds nothing). The backend builds what the reference snapshot ([forcing] reference) binds: the atmosphere (tas and pr, with the elevation zs) and/or the ocean (to, optionally so). An ocean-only reference serves the ocean of the rembo climate; climate = "snapshots" needs the atmosphere. Checked at start-up, with an error naming the group:

every snapshot of a term binds the fields the term lists, and no snapshot binds a field the reference does not;
a snapshot with tas or pr binds zs (the sea-level reduction), except the snap1 of a term without snap0 (below); pr with zs needs tas; so needs to; the reference binds tas and pr together;
the number of groups: tas one (monthly = True) or two (annual mean and one season); pr one or two summed (monthly, e.g. snowfall + rainfall) or one (annual); every other field one.

Seasons. A snapshot with two tas groups (annual mean ta_ann and one season ta_seas) builds the monthly cycle as a cosine with its extremes in January and July, c(m) = cos(2π(m-1)/12): with tas_season = "djf", tas(m) = ta_ann + (ta_seas - ta_ann) c(m) (the season in January); with "jja", tas(m) = ta_ann - (ta_seas - ta_ann) c(m) (in July). The default is the summer of the hemisphere (jja north, djf south), so the second field of CLIMBER-3α (JJA only) serves the south as its winter, and PMIP3 offers both (t2m_jja, t2m_djf).
Ocean. to and so are depth profiles, interpolated to the model depth axis (23 levels, 0-3000 m). A monthly climatology (12 slices, e.g. ORAS5) is averaged to the annual mean; an annual field (one slice: no time axis, e.g. the CLIMBER ocean products, or one record) is taken as is. Without so, the salinity is 0.
Composition. Each term with the snapshots pattern adds to the reference with the weight a_k, the value of its series; the rule is fixed by field:



field
now




tas, to, so
ref + sum_k a_k (snap1_k - snap0_k)


pr
ref * prod_k (1 + a_k (snap1_k/snap0_k - 1))



A term with snap0 = "" adds its snap1 snapshot as the anomaly itself: ref + a_k snap1_k (tas) or ref (1 + a_k (snap1_k - 1)) (pr), e.g. a reconstructed temperature anomaly or precipitation ratio (Badgeley et al., 2020) without a zero snapshot. Such a snapshot binds no zs: its fields are taken as given, so they must be sea-level anomalies or ratios (there is no elevation correction of their own). If it binds zs, it is reduced to sea level like any other snapshot.
&term_b20                     ! input/forcing_db.nml
    snap0  = ""
    snap1  = "b20"            ! snapshot binding tas (anomaly) and pr (ratio), no zs
    fields = "pr"             ! series = "": the constant 1
/
Two terms give the orbital + millennial decomposition of Banderas et al. (2018), e.g. orbital on picontrol -> lgm and millennial on lgm_weak -> lgm_strong, each on its own series; several terms may share one series:
&forcing
    reference = "pd"
    series    = "alpha" "beta"
    terms     = "orbital" "millennial"
/

&series_alpha
    method      = "series"
    series_file = "input/alpha_orbital_r2020.dat"
    norm_t0     = 0.0             ! [yr] series 0 here
    norm_t1     = -21e3           ! [yr] series 1 here (or a window, e.g. -23e3 -19e3: the mean)
/

&series_beta
    method      = "series"
    series_file = "input/beta_ngrip_millennial.dat"
/

&term_orbital
    series = "alpha"
    snap0  = "picontrol"
    snap1  = "lgm"
    fields = "tas" "pr"
/

&term_millennial
    series = "beta"
    snap0  = "lgm_weak"
    snap1  = "lgm_strong"
    fields = "tas" "pr"
/
Turning a proxy series into an index is done by tsgen (norm_t0/norm_t1, see the fesm-utils tsgen docs); a steady state is a const series (df_dt_max = 0, value f_min), independent of the model time.
Uniform terms (pattern = "uniform") add f_ta a to tas (and multiply pr by exp(β_p f_ta a)), f_to a to to and f_so a to so on the fields they list. The ocean anomaly from the atmosphere is a derived series (method = "derived", from = "air_anomaly": factor times the mean sea-level air temperature anomaly of the same update over region, without lag and without the lapse-rate cooling of the ice sheet) with a uniform term on to, the library series_dTo + term_ocean; to without terms stays at the reference. The ocean terms are applied after the atmosphere (a derived series may drive ocean fields only).
The backend holds no state of its own: the series restart with the driver (series_<name>_restart.nc). The climate output carries the value of each term’s series, term_<name>.
The transient forcing is added on top in every configuration.

title: ESM forcing
text: Runs forced by Earth-System-Model (ESM) output (ISMIP7, TIPMIP, 1pctCO2) use the yelmox program with the ESM climate backend: [comps] climate = "esm". The backend wraps libs/esm_forcing.f90: a reference climatology at the current surface (lapse rate, precipitation scaling), plus ESM anomalies over historical and projection periods, optional climate variability and subglacial discharge.

title: ESM forcing
text:
Configuration

Run phase and calendar. [ctrl] run_step names the group holding the timeline ("spinup" or "transient"), with calendar = True and calendar_ref = 2000.0: the timeline is in calendar years. The same group holds the ESM periods (time_ref, time_hist, time_proj, time_esm_ref) and the variability switches (clim_var, clim_seed).
Experiment. [esm]: par_file (the ESM data configuration in input/esm/), experiment and esm_name (the {experiment} and {gcm} of its file paths), use_esm / use_var / use_hist / use_proj, basins (the basins of the ocean extrapolation), and the physical parameters lapse (annual mean and summer lapse rate; the monthly lapse rate follows a seasonal cosine), f_p (precipitation scaled by exp(f_p dT) with the temperature change dT of the elevation correction), f_ocn, f_polar, dT_threshold.
Anomalies. In the spin-up the backend applies the reference climatology only. In a transient run (run_step = "transient") with use_esm = True and experiment other than "ctrl", it reads the ESM groups of the par_file and adds anomalies relative to the mean over time_esm_ref: up to time_hist(2) from the historical groups, from time_proj(1) on from the projection groups. Air temperature and smb anomalies are differences, precipitation a ratio, the ocean anomalies are annual means taken at the shelf base. 1pctCO2 and TIPMIP point the reference and projection groups at the same file. With use_esm = False, experiment = "1pctCO2" instead applies a spatially uniform anomaly (a linear warming of 17 K from 1995 to 2300, capped at dT_threshold, times f_polar; the ocean f_ocn times that); f_ocn, f_polar and dT_threshold act only there.
Forcing on other grids. A field group of the par_file is normally read on the climate grid. With remap (a kernel: bilinear, shepard, nn, quadrant, con) and grid_src (a name for the file’s grid, e.g. "{gcm}-atm") it is read on its own grid and remapped online: a projected grid with a cdo description grid_<grid_src>.txt next to the file (as FesmData writes it) or in maps/, a regular lon-lat grid from its 1D axes (the map is cached in maps/), or a curvilinear grid (e.g. a tripolar ocean) from the 2D lon/lat named in the variable’s coordinates attribute. fill = "nearest" fills the missing values from the nearest valid cell. The 1pctCO2 configs read the global CMIP fields this way, and the Greenland configs the ORAS5 reference ocean, which FesmData provides on GRL-16KM and GRL-32KM only, from GRL-16KM.
Surface mass balance. [comps] surface_method = "climate" takes the ESM’s own SMB (reference + anomaly, corrected from the present-day surface with the SMB elevation gradient); "chion" (the default) or "smbpal" computes it from the ESM temperature and precipitation.
Update cadence. [comps] dt_clim = 1.0: the forcing is updated every step. The spin-up scripts pass comps.dt_clim=10: the forcing of a spin-up is a fixed climatology, so only the geometry correction changes between updates.
Cold start. [sim] init_kill_shelves (no ice where the present-day bed is ocean) and init_time_thrm (equilibration with topography fixed), shared with the other configurations.

title: ESM forcing
ESM forcing
text:
Output
The shared per-module files (yelmo.nc, isos.nc, mshlf.nc, chion.nc, …), plus, with [output] write_clim, esm.nc (the ESM fields on the climate grid) and esm_ts.nc (the forcing averaged over the ice and the floating ice), and, with [output] write_cmip (every dt_cmip), the CMIP-formatted yelmo_cmip.nc and yelmo_ts_cmip.nc.

title: REMBO climate
text: Runs with REMBOv1, an energy/moisture-balance regional atmosphere with an integrated surface-mass-balance scheme, use the yelmox program with the REMBO climate backend: [comps] climate = "rembo". REMBO supplies the atmosphere and the surface mass balance; the ocean comes from the snapshot backend.

title: REMBO climate
text:
Configuration

Grid. REMBO runs on the grid it was compiled for (Greenland, GRL-16KM), which must be grid_clim; the backend checks this at start-up.
Surface mass balance. [comps] surface_method = "climate": REMBO’s smb and surface temperature, at the current surface; any other surface_method stops the run at start-up (REMBO gives annual fields only).
Update cadence. [comps] dt_clim = dtt (10 yr): REMBO updates its energy balance and its smb on its own intervals (dtime_emb = 100, dtime_smb = 1 in rembo_Greenland.nml), with the insolation at the forcing time time_rel.
Ocean. The snapshot backend (see Snapshots) with an ocean-only reference snapshot: [forcing] reference = "pd", the pd snapshot binding the ORAS5 1981-2010 climatology (oras5_1981_2010_to, oras5_1981_2010_so of input/clim_db.nml). The reference must bind to and no atmosphere (checked at start-up); so is optional (salinity 0 without it). The ocean takes the ocean terms of [forcing] as for the snapshots backend (a uniform term on to, e.g. series = "hyst", f_to = 0.25).
Transient forcing. The uniform terms on tas ([term_<name>] pattern = "uniform") are an input of REMBO, not applied after it: their sum f_ta·f is REMBO’s summer air temperature anomaly dT_sum, the annual dT_ann = 1.3·dT_sum (REMBO’s winter factor 1.6); pr in their fields has no effect (REMBO computes the precipitation). Snapshot terms on the atmosphere are refused. Off in the par file ([forcing] series = "", terms = "").
Transforms. [taper] and [bias] are refused at start-up (no reference atmosphere, annual fields only); so is a derived air_anomaly series (no sea-level air temperature).
Cold start. REMBO is equilibrated (10 years) before its first update.

title: REMBO climate
text:
Output
The shared per-module files (yelmo.nc, isos.nc, mshlf.nc, …), plus, with [output] write_clim, rembo.nc (annual and summer air temperature, precipitation, smb, surface temperature, ocean profiles) and rembo_ts.nc (the applied anomalies, the smb integrated over the ice sheet and the accumulation-area ratio). The series go to the Yelmo 1D file (series_<name>), as for the other climates. The library holds the hysteresis setup, series_hyst (PI42 with kill switch) and the uniform term_hyst on tas and pr: -p forcing.series=hyst forcing.terms=hyst runs it (a second uniform term on to for the ocean). Restart bundles hold REMBO’s rembo_restart.nc; REMBO reads its restart as set in rembo_Greenland.nml.

title: What configme install yelmox does
text:
What configme install yelmox does
This page is for context only. The recommended way to install YelmoX is to run configme install yelmox (see the Quick start); you do not need to run any of the commands below by hand. They are reproduced here so you can see exactly what configme clones, configures, links, and builds on your behalf.
configme install performs the following phases:

Clone the YelmoX checkout and each component repository it needs (fesm-utils, yelmo, FastIsostasy, rembo1, chion, insol).
Manifest — write .configme/manifest.toml so the checkout is self-describing regardless of its directory name.
Link each component into the directories where the build expects it.
Configure — generate a system-specific Makefile for every package from shared machine/compiler fragments, with the netCDF paths detected automatically.
Build fesm-utils (LIS + FFTW + utils). This is the slow step (~10-30 min), which is why it is folded into the install rather than run separately.
Extras — install runme if it is missing, create .runme_config, and link the external data paths (ice_data, fesmdata, isostasy_data).

Each run also writes the exact commands it executed to a .install.sh script in the checkout, so any install is reproducible. The script below is the equivalent for the dkrz_levante machine with the ifx compiler; substitute your own machine and compiler, and note that the netCDF paths (NC_FROOT / NC_CROOT) and the install root are filled in automatically for your system.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generated by `configme install` — reproduces this install.
set -euo pipefail
# target=yelmox  machine=dkrz_levante  compiler=ifx

# --- clone ---
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/yelmox.git $YELMOXROOT
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/fesm-utils.git $YELMOXROOT/fesm-utils
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/yelmo.git $YELMOXROOT/yelmo
git clone git@github.com:palma-ice/FastIsostasy.git $YELMOXROOT/FastIsostasy
git clone git@github.com:alex-robinson/rembo1.git $YELMOXROOT/rembo1

# --- manifest ---
mkdir -p $YELMOXROOT/.configme  # write .configme/manifest.toml

# --- links ---
ln -s ../fesm-utils $YELMOXROOT/yelmo/fesm-utils
ln -s ../fesm-utils $YELMOXROOT/FastIsostasy/fesm-utils
ln -s ../fesm-utils $YELMOXROOT/rembo1/fesm-utils

# --- configure (per package) ---
# fesm-utils: build with autotools (slow, ~10-30 min):
(cd $YELMOXROOT/fesm-utils && NC_FROOT=<auto-detected> NC_CROOT=<auto-detected> ./build.py --variant both -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)
(cd $YELMOXROOT/fesm-utils/utils && configme config fesm-utils/utils -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)
# fesm-utils/utils: build (serial, omp):
(cd $YELMOXROOT/fesm-utils/utils && make openmp=0 fesmutils-static)
(cd $YELMOXROOT/fesm-utils/utils && make openmp=1 fesmutils-static)
(cd $YELMOXROOT/yelmo && configme config yelmo -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)
(cd $YELMOXROOT/FastIsostasy && configme config FastIsostasy -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)
(cd $YELMOXROOT/rembo1 && configme config rembo1 -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)
(cd $YELMOXROOT && configme config yelmox -m dkrz_levante -c ifx)

# --- extras ---
command -v runme >/dev/null 2>&1 || pip install git+https://github.com/fesmc/runme
# runme_config: create .runme_config and set hpc/account
runme --config  # or: cp .runme/runme_config .runme_config
# data_link ice_data: ln -s <path> ice_data
# data_link fesmdata: ln -s <$FESMDATA> fesmdata   (FesmData v2 products, e.g. /work/ba1442/fesmdata)
# data_link isostasy_data: ln -s <path> isostasy_data

title: 1pctCO2
text: Greenland and Antarctic simulations under the idealized CMIP experiment 1pctCO2 (atmospheric CO2 rising by 1 %/yr, about 4xCO2 after 140 yr), in two steps: a present-day optimization spin-up, as for ISMIP7, then the scenario, which starts from the spin-up’s restart bundle and runs 140 yr under the absolute CMIP fields of one GCM, taken relative to their own first years.

title: 1pctCO2
text:
Spin-up
The spin-up passes ctrl.run_step=spinup comps.dt_clim=10 sim.relax=True sim.opt=True esm.experiment=ctrl. It is the ISMIP7 spin-up (same [spinup], [relax] and [opt] groups) except for the surface mass balance, which chion computes from the reference climate ([comps] surface_method = "chion"; ISMIP7 takes the ESM’s own smb). In the spin-up the backend applies the reference climatology only.
opt_ant.sh is a tuned 20-kyr Antarctic optimization spin-up on ANT-16KM with yelmox_esm_Antarctica.nml, ismip7_ant and pct_ant: cb_ref started from the till friction of the bed (opt.cf_init=-1), a short relaxation (relax.time1/2 = 100), the ocean extrapolated into the shelves (marine_shelf.extrap_shlf=True), equilibrium calving, DIVA, shelf enhancement 0.5. Output in output/1pctCO2/opt-ANT-16KM-l21-bedmap3.

title: 1pctCO2
text:
Scenario

Timeline: [transient] 2020 to 2160 on the calendar clock ([ctrl] calendar = True, tstep_method = "cal", dtt = 1 yr): the start of the experiment (about 1xCO2) is 2020, the end 140 yr later.
Switches: ctrl.run_step=transient esm.experiment=1pctCO2 esm.esm_name=<GCM> esm.use_esm=True esm.use_hist=False esm.use_proj=True, ctrl.restart = <OUTROOT>/spinup/restart-<SPINUP_YEARS/1e3>-kyr (absolute path).
Periods: time_esm_ref = 2020, 2021, time_proj = 2020, 2160; time_hist = 2018, 2019 lies before time_init, so every step reads the projection.

title: Antarctica
text: Antarctic test cases in the present-day climate (RACMO2.3p2 1981–2010, ISMIP7 ocean) with the snapshot backend: a 15-kyr spin-up at 32 km that optimizes the basal friction (cb_ref) and the ocean thermal-forcing correction (tf_corr), with the marine shelf on a 16 km grid (yelmox_Antarctica.nml, the base of a multigrid resolution test), and a 50-kyr present-day run at 32 km without optimization (the same par file with -p overrides). Two variants run on the ESM backend (yelmox_esm_Antarctica.nml, alone and with the nudge setup of scripts/nudge/run_nudge_antarctica.sh).

title: Antarctica
text:
Running
From the yelmox root:
runme -rs -q compute -w 02:00:00 --omp 16 -e yelmox -n yelmox/yelmox_Antarctica.nml -o output/ant
runme -rs -q compute -w 08:00:00 --omp 16 -e yelmox -n yelmox/yelmox_Antarctica.nml -o output/ant-pd \
      -p ctrl.time_end=50e3 sim.relax=False sim.opt=False domain.grid_hub=ANT-32KM domain.grid_ice="" \
         domain.grid_shelf=ANT-32KM marine_shelf.tf_correction=True tm_2D.dt=500 tm_2Dsm.dt=500
On a busy queue, run them as chains of short jobs (Long runs in chunks). The multigrid resolution test, from anywhere; run_mg_forward.sh needs the restart bundles of run_mg_resolution.sh:
yelmox/run_mg_resolution.sh
yelmox/run_mg_cfmin.sh
yelmox/run_mg_forward.sh
The scripts submit by default (runopts=-r runs locally, runopts=-s stages only). The climate always runs on ANT-32KM; Yelmo, isostasy and the surface on the Yelmo grid; the hub and the marine shelf on the shelf grid.

run_mg_resolution.sh: six 25-kyr spin-ups (ctrl.time_end=25e3) into output/mg_opt/y<ice>_m<shelf>: Yelmo and shelf on the same grid (ANT-8KM, ANT-16KM, ANT-32KM), and the shelf on a finer grid (Yelmo 32 km with shelf 8 or 16 km, Yelmo 16 km with shelf 8 km). 2D output every 1 kyr, ytopo.gz_Hg1=100; shared queue, 10 h.
run_mg_cfmin.sh: the three Yelmo-32KM spin-ups again with the friction floor ytill.cf_min=1e-4 (par file: 0.01), into output/mg_opt_cfmin1e-4; compute queue, 8 h.
run_mg_forward.sh: 1-kyr runs from restart-25.000-kyr of the three Yelmo-32KM spin-ups in output/mg_opt (a missing bundle is skipped), with sim.relax=False, sim.opt=False, yelmo.restart_relax=0: ctrl (no anomaly) and warm (+2 K air and ocean temperature: the uniform term [term_dT] on the constant series [series_dT], f_ta = 1, f_to = 1), into output/mg_fwd/<case>_<ctrl|warm>; compute queue, 4 h.

title: Antarctica
text:
Spin-up

Timeline: [ctrl] 0 to 15 kyr, dtt = 10 yr, the forcing held at present day (tstep_method = "const", tstep_const = 0), present-day insolation ([orbit] method = "time", time = 0); the sea level follows the model’s own ice-volume change ([barysealevel] method = "fastiso").
Cold start: a 10-yr equilibration ([sim] init_method = "equil", init_equil_time = 10).
Optimization ([sim] opt = True): cb_ref (opt_cf = "L21", from cf_init = 1e-2 everywhere) and tf_corr per point (opt_tf = "L21-points", tf_sigma = 50 km, within ±1 K), both until 15 kyr ([opt] cf_time_end, tf_time_end); the grounding line and grounding zone relax towards the observations until 6 kyr ([sim] relax = True, [relax] topo_rel = 4, tau1 = 100 yr until 2 kyr, then towards tau2 = 2000 yr).
Basin corrections: [marine_shelf] corr_method = "tf", corr_names = "b1" "b12" "b14" "b15", corr_values = 0.3 0.3 -1.5 0.0 on the Zwally2012 basins 1 (Ronne), 12 (Ross), 14 (Pine Island) and 15 (Abbott); corr_b<k> selects basin k.
Output: 1D every year, 2D every 200 yr, small 2D every 50 yr.

title: Greenland paleo
text: Greenland paleo simulations on the GreenlandPaleo domain (GRL-PAL, 16 km), the Greenland domain extended 640 km to the west (Ellesmere, Devon Island, Baffin Bay). Two setups, without optimization of the basal friction or the ocean thermal forcing:

title: Greenland paleo
text:
Running
Run from the yelmox root; each transient needs the last restart bundle of its spin-up.
A:
scripts/grl-paleo/run_spinup.sh pd 0 output/grl-paleo/spinup-pd-0ka sim.relax=True
scripts/grl-paleo/run_lgp.sh
B:
scripts/grl-paleo/run_spinup.sh recon -21e3
scripts/grl-paleo/run_deglac.sh
run_spinup.sh <forcing> <time> [output_path] [extra -p ...] runs 20 kyr with the forcing grlpal_<forcing> (pd, lgp or recon) held at <time> (ctrl.tstep_const, yr: climate, insolation, sea level). The ice starts from the present-day topography at time 0 and from GLAC-1D at <time> otherwise; the output goes to output/grl-paleo/spinup-<forcing>-<ka>ka by default. Any setup can so be spun up at the present day or at the LGM, e.g. the steady state of B under present-day forcing: run_spinup.sh recon 0. run_lgp.sh [spinup_path] [output_path] restarts from <spinup_path>/restart-20.000-kyr (default spinup-pd-0ka) and writes to output/grl-paleo/lgp; run_deglac.sh [lgm_path] [output_path] restarts from <lgm_path>/restart-20.000-kyr (default spinup-recon-21ka) and writes to output/grl-paleo/deglac (the bundles are passed as absolute paths; the scripts stop if one is missing). All submit to the shared queue (2 days, 10 GB, no OpenMP). On a busy cluster, run them as chains of short jobs instead: Long runs in chunks has the commands.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
Domain borders
The west border cuts Baffin Island and the Canadian Arctic Archipelago, where Innuitian and Laurentide ice crosses it in glacial periods. The borders are “infinite” ([yelmo] experiment = "infinite", mask_border = "dynamic"): the outermost cells take the thickness of their inner neighbours, so the border ice thickens and thins with the interior. Ice flows out through the border but not in: the ice west of the border is what the local climate builds. The reset of the border cells is booked in mb_border; the domain totals in yelmo_ts.nc leave these cells out, and mb_border_tot is their total (the outflow). Before Yelmo fixed this (2026-10-19), the border cells fed the interior wherever the flow pointed inwards, without limit and unbooked; in the first B LGM spin-up this inflow grew exponentially (above the domain SMB after ~8 kyr) and piled ice up to 10 km at the front in northern Baffin Bay.
Prescribed border ice is the alternative (not used now): a strip of fixed and relaxation cells ([yelmo_masks] border_width = N M, e.g. 2 4) whose thickness comes from an ice history ([ice_bnd] active = True, PaleoMIST by default), with experiment = "None", mask_border = "auto" and [ytopo] topo_rel = -1.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
Reference climate
ERA5 1981–2010 (monthly) is the present-day reference on the whole domain; MAR v3.14 covers only Greenland. Over Greenland, [bias] corrects ERA5 to MAR 1981–2010 with a monthly temperature difference dtas and precipitation factor fpr, both taken at sea level with the reduction of the snapshot backend ([snapshots] lapse, f_p), so they do not depend on elevation. Outside the MAR coverage the correction is the nearest value of the bias smoothed over 50 km, tapered to zero over 100 km (cosine). fpr is clamped to [0.2, 5].
The product is a hand-built file in ice_data, ice_data/GreenlandPaleo/GRL-PAL-16KM/GRL-PAL-16KM_BIAS-MARv3.14-ERA5-1981-2010.nc (clim_db.nml groups bias_mar_era5_1981_2010_dtas, _fpr), made by
julia --project=scripts/grl-paleo scripts/grl-paleo/make_bias_mar_era5.jl --fig
from the yelmox root (fesmdata and ice_data links in place; options --res, --l1, --l2, --f_p, --D, --sigma, --fpr_min, --fpr_max). The lapse rates and f_p are written as attributes: remake the file when [snapshots] lapse or f_p change.



Present-day climate of yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml (ERA5 1981–2010 with the MAR – ERA5 bias), climate-only run: annual and summer air temperature, annual precipitation.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
A. Spin-up

Timeline: [ctrl] 0 to 15 kyr, dtt = 10 yr, present-day insolation ([orbit] method = "fixed_time", time = 0), sea level from file at 0 ka.
No optimization ([sim] opt = False); the ice thickness relaxes towards the observations until 6 kyr ([sim] relax = True, [relax] time2).
Climate: present day (forcing.series="", forcing.terms="") with the MAR – ERA5 bias.
Output: restart bundles at 0 and 15 kyr; 2D output every 1 kyr.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
A. Transient

Timeline: [ctrl] -130 kyr to 0, dtt = 10 yr, on relative time (tstep_method = "rel"). [sim] relax = False, opt = False.
Climate: the present-day reference plus the term glacial ([term_glacial], picontrol -> lgm on tas and pr): the PMIP3 LGM – piControl anomaly scaled by the series glacial ([series_glacial], input/alpha_combined_125kyr_interp.dat, as is: 0 = present day, ~0.9 at 21 ka, -0.2 in the last interglacial). The term ocean adds the derived series dTo, 0.25 times the mean sea-level air temperature anomaly. Insolation varies in time ([orbit] method = "forcing_time").
Sea level: [barysealevel] method = "file", input/sealevel_spratt2016.dat.




Forcing of yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml with grlpal_lgp of scripts/grl-paleo/params.sh at 21 ka and 125 ka minus present day, climate-only run on present-day topography: annual and summer air temperature difference, precipitation ratio.



Ice age: isochrones with elsa ([ytrc] use_elsa, [elsa_grl_lgp] of input/forcing_db.nml): one layer every 1 kyr, coupled every 50 yr (for comparison with MacGregor et al., 2025).
Output: 2D every 1 kyr, 1D every 100 yr, restart bundles every 25 kyr.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
B. Reconstruction forcing
The reference pd plus two terms without a series (the constant 1), one per field (forcing.terms==b18,b20,ocean):

Temperature, term b18 ([term_b18] on tas): the Buizert et al.

monthly reconstruction (snapshot_b18, decadal, 22 ka to 2005 CE) minus its 1981–2010 baseline (snapshot_b18_base), both at the reconstruction’s elevation.

Precipitation, term b20 ([term_b20] on pr): the Badgeley et al. (2020) fraction relative to 1850–2000 CE (snapshot_b20, snap0 = "": the snapshot is the ratio itself; 50-yr means, 20 ka to 0; annual, the same factor in every month). b20_pr_frac_low/_high are the other accumulation scenarios.

Swapping the fields of the two terms gives the other combinations (Badgeley temperature: its annual anomaly in every month). The time-varying groups are read in time at the forcing time (extrap: the first slice before the record starts, e.g. Badgeley at 20 ka during the LGM spin-up).
The reconstructions are GRL-16KM products, remapped online onto GRL-PAL and filled from the nearest cell outside the GRL box. [taper] with outside = "mean" replaces the anomaly there by the mean anomaly of the coverage (per month: the temperature difference and the precipitation ratio of the totals, recomputed at every climate update): w = 1 in the coverage of both, a cosine to 0 over 100 km (hand-built file ice_data/GreenlandPaleo/GRL-PAL-16KM/GRL-PAL-16KM_TAPER-Buizert2018-Badgeley2020.nc, clim_db.nml group taper_b18_b20, made by scripts/grl-paleo/make_taper_recon.jl). West of it (Ellesmere, Baffin Bay) the climate is the present-day reference plus that mean anomaly.
The ocean anomaly is the term ocean, 0.25 times the mean sea-level air temperature anomaly (the derived series dTo); sea level from input/sealevel_spratt2016.dat (as A); insolation at the forcing time ([orbit] method = "forcing_time"). The climate is updated every 100 yr (dt_clim; the reconstructions are read and remapped from GRL-16KM at each update, which made 10 yr six times slower).



Forcing of yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml with grlpal_recon of scripts/grl-paleo/params.sh at 21 ka and 12.5 ka minus present day, climate-only run on present-day topography: annual and summer air temperature difference, precipitation ratio. West of the GRL box: the mean anomaly of the reconstructions.

title: Greenland paleo
text:
B. LGM spin-up

Timeline: [ctrl] 0 to 20 kyr, the forcing held at 21 ka (tstep_method = "const", tstep_const = -21e3): reconstructions, insolation and sea level of 21 ka.

The imposed ice is smoothed (Gaussian, 2 dx), floating ice thinner than 50 m is removed, and the result becomes the reference thickness H_ice_ref; the dynamics are then stabilized for 200 yr with beta_min = 100 Pa a m-1 (domain_init_recon, libs/kryos_startup.f90). title: Laurentide LGM
text:
Surface mass balance
Laurentide, [comps] surface_method = "smb_simple", synthetic-elevation scheme ([smb_simple] scheme = "syn", libs/smb_simple.f90). The SMB is evaluated on a synthetic surface elevation built from the distance to the margin of a target ice mask (plastic profile inside, tau0 = 36 kPa):
smb  = acc - abl,   acc = c0 exp(-d_in/L_acc),   abl = beta (z_SL - z)  (z < z_SL)
z_SL = a1 + a2 phi,   beta = beta0 + beta1 (phiref - phi)
with c0 = 300 mm w.e./yr, L_acc = 300 km, a1 = 3900 m, a2 = -50 m/degN, beta0 = 5 (mm/yr)/m at phiref = 60 degN, beta1 = 0.05. Outside the mask the SMB is at most smb_min = -2000 mm w.e./yr. The mask is ice_data/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_Batchelor2019_ice_masks.nc ({grid_name} = grid_surface: LIS-32KM), slice mask_idx = 18 (LGM; 14–17: 45, 40, 35, 30 ka). The climate enters only through the sea-level air temperature: t_srf = t_sl - gamma_t z_syn (gamma_t = 6.5e-3 K/m), capped at 273.15 K inside the mask.

title: YelmoX
text:
YelmoX is the driver framework around the Yelmo ice-sheet model. It bundles Yelmo together with the libraries needed to run realistic ice-sheet simulations: climate and ocean forcing modules, the FastIsostasy bedrock module, the REMBOv1 energy/moisture-balance model, and shared utilities from fesm-utils.
For documentation of the Yelmo ice-sheet model itself, see the Yelmo docs.


With configme installed (see Install configme below), build the whole YelmoX stack with a single command from the directory where you want the checkout to live:
configme install yelmox
That’s it, you should now be ready to compile and run any yelmox program:
make clean
make yelmox



configme install yelmox clones YelmoX and its component repositories (fesm-utils, yelmo, FastIsostasy, rembo1, chion, insol), configures each for your machine and compiler, links them into the YelmoX directory, and builds fesm-utils (LIS + FFTW + utils, which can take 10-30 min). If configme can detect your machine from the hostname it does so, otherwise it prompts you.
The only system dependency you must install yourself is netCDF (see the Yelmo dependencies notes for installation tips). Everything else — LIS, FFTW, the fesm-utils libraries, the component repositories, their links, and runme — is managed by configme.
Common options:
configme install yelmox -m dkrz_levante -c ifx   # pick the machine + compiler explicitly
configme install yelmox -d https                 # clone over HTTPS (no GitHub SSH key needed)
configme install yelmox --dir ~/models/yelmox    # put the checkout here instead of ./yelmox
configme install yelmox --overwrite              # re-clone over an existing checkout
configme install yelmox --build-deps             # rebuild dependency packages without prompting
Run configme list for the supported machines and compilers, and configme --help for the full command surface. The exact clone/configure/link/build commands configme install yelmox runs for you are recorded in a .install.sh script in the checkout, and are also shown for context on the configme install details page — these are shown for reference only; configme install is the recommended path and you do not need to run them by hand.



configme install yelmox already clones the repository for you, so most users do not need this step. If you want to fetch the YelmoX source tree by hand (for example, to inspect it before installing), the repository is here: https://github.com/fesmc/yelmox.
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/yelmox.git
cd yelmox



YelmoX is configured and built with configme, a small Python tool that detects your netCDF installation, configures every package in the stack for your machine and compiler, and clones/links/builds the whole thing with one command. It is installed once, globally, and provides the configme command on your PATH:
pip install git+https://github.com/fesmc/configme
To upgrade it later, use its built-in update command:
configme update
If the configme command is not found after installation, your Python user bin directory is probably not on your PATH; add it in your ~/.bashrc / ~/.zshrc:
export PATH="${PATH}:${HOME}/.local/bin"

title: Long runs in chunks
text: A long simulation can run as a chain of short jobs (“chunks”) instead of one long job. On a busy cluster short jobs start much sooner (the scheduler fits them into gaps between larger jobs), and a chain of 30-min jobs often finishes long before one 8-hour job starts. The restarts are exact, so the chain gives the same result as one run.

title: Long runs in chunks
text:
How a chunk restarts
The start time of a run comes from its timeline group ([ctrl], or the group named by [ctrl] run_step, e.g. [transient]), not from the restart bundle. Each chunk therefore gets

time_init = the time_end of the previous chunk, and its own time_end;
ctrl.restart = the bundle the previous chunk wrote at its time_end. A run always writes a bundle at time_end, named restart-<time_end/1000, 3 decimals>-kyr (e.g. restart-15.000-kyr, restart--125.000-kyr), so all paths are known when the chain is submitted.

Chunk k runs in its own folder OUTDIR/cNN; the output of the run is split over the chunk folders. Each job waits for the previous one (sbatch --dependency=afterok): if a chunk fails or runs out of time, the rest of the chain is not started (Slurm keeps it pending with reason DependencyNeverSatisfied; cancel it with scancel).
Choose the chunk length so a chunk finishes well within the walltime (RUNOPTS, default 30 min with 16 OpenMP threads); the chunk boundaries should be multiples of the climate, isostasy and output intervals (dt_clim, dt_isos, tm_*), which are counted from the start of each run.

title: Long runs in chunks
section: What changes after the first chunk
text:
What changes after the first chunk
Some settings are timed from the start of a run (time_elapsed), not from the forcing time, and must be set for the later chunks (--p-rest):







Setting
Later chunks




Relaxation ([sim] relax, schedule [relax] time1, time2)
sim.relax=False once the relaxation has ended (let the first chunk cover it)


Optimization ([opt] cf_time_*, tf_time_*)
same: within the first chunk, or sim.opt=False after


elsa isochrones ([ytrc] use_elsa)
ytrc.elsa_restart=True (restore the layers)


Cold-start settings ([sim] init_method, …)
none: a restart skips them



[yelmo] restart_z_bed = True (all configs) takes the bed from the bundle; with False, restart_relax would blend the bed towards the input topography after each restart.

title: Long runs in chunks
Long runs in chunks
text:
Example: Greenland paleo
The two Greenland paleo setups, each a spin-up and a transient, in 5-kyr chunks (the A spin-up in 6, 5, 5 and 4 kyr, so that its first chunk covers the relaxation until 6 kyr). All run on yelmox/yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml, with the overrides of the scripts/grl-paleo/run_*.sh scripts less the times and the restart. Each -p takes one quoted string, so an array of scripts/grl-paleo/params.sh is passed as "${grlpal_lgp[*]}":
source scripts/grl-paleo/params.sh
par=yelmox/yelmox_GreenlandPaleo.nml
elsa="ytrc.use_elsa=True ytrc.t_dep_source=elsa ytrc.elsa_nml=input/forcing_db.nml"
read jA rA < <(scripts/run_chunks.sh -p "tm_1D.dt=10 tm_2D.dt=1000" --p-first "sim.relax=True" $par output/grl-paleo/spinup-pd-0ka 0 6000 11000 16000 20000)
scripts/run_chunks.sh -d "$jA" -r "$rA" -p "${grlpal_lgp[*]}" \
    -p "ctrl.tstep_method=rel tm_1D.dt=100 tm_2D.dt=1000 tm_2Dsm.dt=1000000 $elsa ytrc.elsa_group=elsa_grl_lgp" \
    --p-first "ytrc.elsa_restart=False" --p-rest "ytrc.elsa_restart=True" $par output/grl-paleo/lgp $(seq -130000 5000 0)
read jB rB < <(scripts/run_chunks.sh -p "${grlpal_recon[*]}" \
    -p "ctrl.tstep_const=-21e3 tm_1D.dt=10 tm_2D.dt=1000 sim.init_method=recon sim.recon_var=H_ice sim.recon_time=-21e3 sim.recon_regions=all" \
    -p "sim.recon_path=fesmdata/{domain}/{grid_name}/{grid_name}_IceHistory-GLAC1D.nc" \
    $par output/grl-paleo/spinup-recon-21ka 0 5000 10000 15000 20000)
scripts/run_chunks.sh -d "$jB" -r "$rB" -p "${grlpal_recon[*]}" \
    -p "ctrl.tstep_method=rel comps.dt_clim=100 tm_1D.dt=10 tm_2D.dt=500 tm_2Dsm.dt=100 $elsa ytrc.elsa_group=elsa_grl_deglac" \
    --p-first "ytrc.elsa_restart=False" --p-rest "ytrc.elsa_restart=True" $par output/grl-paleo/deglac -21000 -16000 -11000 -6000 -1000 0
The first command chain is 4 + 26 jobs, the second 4 + 5; all 39 are submitted at once.

title: yelmox_bipolar
text: The two-domain variant of yelmox: it runs a northern and a southern ice-sheet domain together, coupled through a shared barystatic sea level and a shared Ocean Box Model (OBM) that exchanges freshwater flux and ocean temperature between the hemispheres. Each domain is a full kryos_domain, configured as in yelmox with the hemisphere suffix on its groups (see Configuration); the driver interleaves the step_* primitives across both domains plus the OBM.

title: yelmox_bipolar
text:
What’s distinct

Two kryos_domains (dom_north, dom_south), each set up via setup_domain → domain_startup. Either can be individually deactivated (active_north / active_south); with neither, the ocean box model runs alone (active_obm, forced by atm2obm or not; ism2obm off, no terms on the box series).
Shared bsl — one barystatic sea level for the run, restored once at startup (bsl_startup) and written to the run restart bundle.
Shared OBM (obm) — an ocean box model stepped once per timestep, configured via obm_ctl_load and coupled to the domains through obm_coupling.f90 (coupling_obm2ism, obm_coupling_init, obm_exchange). The OBM writes its own 1D output, <obm_name>.nc ([ctrl] obm_name, nautilus or stommel), on the [tm_1D] cadence; its restart (obm_restart.nc) goes into the run restart bundle next to bsl_restart.nc.
One restart bundle per run — restart-<kyr>-kyr/ holds the shared bsl_restart.nc, obm_restart.nc and the series (series_<name>_restart.nc), and each domain in a subfolder named after it (Greenland/, Antarctica/). [ctrl] restart is the bundle to start from. The output of each domain goes to the same subfolder of the run folder.

Climate/SMB per domain is snapshots + chion ([chion_north] model = "itm", [chion_south] model = "pdd"), as in the single-domain driver; the OBM’s contribution is folded into the ocean forcing — obm_exchange sets the derived series obm_north/obm_south (the box temperatures) and re-applies each domain’s ocean terms (e.g. the replace terms term_obm_north/_south: the box temperature into to_ann) before the marine-shelf step reads it.

title: yelmox_bipolar
text:
Stepping order
Main loop (per timestep):
call bsl_update(bsl, ts%time_rel)              ! shared sea level, once
call indices_update(idx, ts%time_rel, var=fvar) ! shared series, once (fvar: ice volume of the active domains [Gt])

if (active_north) then                         ! relaxation + optimization + isostasy, per domain
    call step_relax(dom_north, ts)
    call step_optimize(dom_north, ts)
    call step_isostasy(dom_north, ts, bsl)
end if
(same for dom_south)

if (oc%active_obm) call obm_update(obox, real(dtt,wp), oc%obm_name)   ! ocean box model, one step

if (active_north) then                         ! ice sheet, hub, climate + smb, per domain
    call couple_to_yelmo(dom_north)
    call step_ice_bnd(dom_north, ts, idx)
    call step_icesheet(dom_north, ts)
    call couple_yelmo_to_htopo(dom_north)
    call step_climate(dom_north, ts, idx)
    call step_surface(dom_north, ts)
end if
(same for dom_south)

call obm_exchange(oc, obox, idx, dom_north, dom_south, ...)  ! atm->obm, ism->obm freshwater,
                                                            ! hysteresis forcing, obm->ism (the obm_* series, ocean terms)

if (active_north) call step_shelf(dom_north, ts)  ! reads the obm-updated to_ann
if (active_south) call step_shelf(dom_south, ts)
Key ordering points:

Isostasy for both domains runs before the OBM step, so the OBM sees a consistent geometry.
obm_update uses the previous step’s atmospheric/freshwater forcing (a one-step lag), then obm_exchange distributes the fresh OBM state back to the domains before the marine-shelf melt is computed.
The per-domain primitives are the same as in the single-domain yelmox; only the relaxation + optimization + isostasy part is split off so it runs before the OBM step.

title: yelmox_bipolar
text:
Forcing
One global series drives the box model and, with regional gains, the domains (yelmox_bipolar_Bipolar.nml):

Series ([forcing] series, [series_<name>]) are shared by both domains and the OBM: advanced once per step, written to each domain’s 1D file, restarted from the run bundle (series_<name>_restart.nc), with the kill switch and restart_every_df bundles as in yelmox. Here orbital (the orbital index of the north’s term orbital), gmt (global mean air temperature anomaly [K], const 0; a file series instead for a transient) and dTo (derived, the north’s ocean anomaly). The reference and the terms of each domain are [forcing_north] and [forcing_south].
atm2obm ([ctrl]): the box air temperatures from [obm_forcing], theta_i = theta_i_init + ampl_i × gain × index for north, tropics and south (ampl_i: [nautilus] thermal_ampl_*, Zickfeld et al., 2004) and the vapour fluxes phin, phit linear in it. It needs no ice-sheet domain; the series must be in the registry (checked at init).
Domains: the uniform terms regional_north/regional_south on gmt with f_ta the regional amplification (north 1.07, south 0.86): explicit in the par file, zero while gmt = 0. North: pd_grl plus the term orbital (picontrol -> lgm) and the term ocean (the derived series dTo); south: pd_ant only.
obm2ism: per domain, a series derived from the box ([series_obm_north], [series_obm_south] of the library: method = "derived", from = "obm_north"/"obm_south", the box temperature, or its anomaly to the initial value with anomaly = True) with a term on to ([term_obm_north]/[term_obm_south]: replace, to_ann = the box temperature; a uniform term with the anomaly series for the reference + the box anomaly). obm_exchange sets the series and re-applies the ocean terms after both climate steps. At the start the box model is initialized (cold start or restart) and the series set before the domains, so their startup climate, shelf and ice state already see the box. It needs active_obm; the series replace dTo (forcing_north.terms==orbital,regional_north,obm_north, see run_tests.sh).
ism2obm: freshwater flux of each domain into the boxes (fn, fs), per hemisphere with [ctrl] couple_fwf_north/couple_fwf_south, from the Yelmo mass balance (fwf_definition: dVdt, mb, ablation) within the hydrographic mask (hydro_mask_north/hydro_mask_south, on the Yelmo grid).
Hysteresis (nautilus only): [nautilus] hyster_on nudges one box-model control (hyster_forcing: phit, phin, fn, fs, global_melt) along hyster_forcing_method (triangular, sin, noise, linear) in obm_exchange.

obm_restart.nc (run bundle) holds the box state, the fluxes and the box air temperatures; the *_init values stay those of the par file, the reference of atm2obm and of the box anomaly (anomaly = True).
